Service: The staff are very friendly and also recommends the Best seller and how to properly eat Vietnamese food. Like don’t be afraid to ask any questions because they’re Very friendly.
Atmosphere: The place is very chill, to nearby hotels and convenience store and it’s just right around the corner by the park.

author: Celina N
review_text: Wonderful place with delicious food! The staff were welcoming, friendly, and attentive. They made sure we were comfortable and enjoying the food. I never tried bun cha and goodness, it was yummy! 😋

author: Narumi M
review_text: The atmosphere was warm and friendly. The owners personally gave us recommendations , especially the salted coffee which was the bomb!! Everything we had was delicious.  They even gave us local eateries and places to see in HCM. I highly recommend folks (local and tourist) to come check them out.

author: yukari liow
review_text: tried the chicken pho from here and the owner recommended me to try the salted coffee, both were absolutely phenomenal!! price was quite affordable too. the owners were really friendly and wholesome, i felt welcomed immediately. would definitely come again just to order their salted coffee!!

author: Kaylee k
review_text: Can’t recommend this place enough!! The food is absolutely delicious, the bun cha takes me straight back to Hanoi! Yen and Carol are also very welcoming and loving. I will definitely be back!

author: Ying Zhou Soo
review_text: Newly opened restaurant in the district. Owner was very friendly and conversant in Viet, English and Mandarin (会说中文). The chicken pho was outstanding. Grilled pork that accompanied the Bun Cha and Banh Mi was out of this world. 100% would recommend you l check this place out!

author: Ines 063
review_text:
A fantastic find in Ho Chi Minh City! The food was incredibly delicious and the portions were a great size for the price. I love that they have plenty of vegetarian options available.
I highly recommend the Vietnamese-style curry with vermicelli—it was packed with fresh vegetables and several types of mushrooms that had a unique and interesting flavor profile. Compliments to the chef!
The restaurant itself is beautifully decorated, creating a lovely local atmosphere, and the staff were exceptionally kind and welcoming. It's also in a perfect location: right near a park and within easy walking distance of Ben Thanh Market. Definitely worth a visit!

author: Andres Al dah dah
review_text: I was craving Bun Thit Nuon and saw this place so I gave it a try. I was pleasantly surprised by how delicious it was! The taste is very similar to the Bun Thit Nuon I had in Ha Noi and the portion size is good too. I’ll come back here again.

author: Ava Alfaro
review_text: Miss Yen, the owner of the restaurant greeted us with a lot of enthusiasm. We only had an afternoon snack here but the banh mi was delicious! I also like their lime tea :) Place has good energy and friendly staff.  We finished our meal quickly!

author: Sammy Six
review_text: Quality food in a well designed environment, just like their other outlet at Hanoi Corner. Super friendly owner, passionate about her products. I had the vegetarian curry with a premium type of mushroom that tasted just like beef, very interesting!

author: Moon Nguyet Tm Vu
review_text:
Hanoi Kitchen truly delivers an authentic taste of Hanoi right in the heart of Ho Chi Minh City. From the very first bite, the food reflects the soul of Northern Vietnamese cuisine—balanced, delicate, and deeply flavorful. Each dish is thoughtfully prepared, using fresh ingredients and traditional recipes that stay true to Hanoi’s culinary heritage. Nothing feels rushed or overly commercial; instead, every plate feels like a respectful homage to home-style Hanoi cooking.

The service is equally impressive. The staff are warm, attentive, and genuinely welcoming, always ready to explain dishes or make recommendations with a smile. Orders are handled efficiently, and the team strikes a perfect balance between being attentive and giving diners space to enjoy their meal.

The atmosphere is another highlight. Hanoi Kitchen offers a cozy, elegant setting that blends classic Hanoi charm with modern comfort. It feels calm, inviting, and ideal for both casual meals and meaningful gatherings. Despite being located in the busy center of Ho Chi Minh City, the restaurant provides a sense of calm and familiarity—almost like stepping into a quiet corner of Hanoi.

Overall, Hanoi Kitchen is a must-visit for anyone who loves authentic Vietnamese cuisine or wants to experience the true flavors of Hanoi without leaving the city. Exceptional food, heartfelt service, and a warm atmosphere make this place well deserving of five stars. 🌟

author: Anh Nguyen
review_text:
I’ve been a regular at the original Nguyen Thi Minh Khai location for a long time; the only real drawback was the limited space. This newly opened branch fixes that problem completely. It’s spacious, has five floors, and the decoration is really cute.
I ordered the Bún Thang and salted coffee, and both were excellent. The soup is aromatic yet light, the ingredients are fresh, and the coffee is spot-on. I’d say the Bún Thang is true to Northern cuisine and so far the best I’ve tasted. Definitely worth the visit.

author: GA EUN AN
review_text: really good taste, like Korean chicken noodle soup. everything goes well with Korean taste, and feel healthy

author: Wing you Tsang
review_text: The owner is so friendly and they have such a great service and the food is so delicious.

author: Tay Huiyi
review_text: Bun Cha was very good, dipping sauce was well made and flavourful, and the meats and meatball were exceptional

author: J. Thomas
review_text: Huge recommendation for Pho and Bun Cha (probably everything else as well)! Lovely owners/staff, explanations how to eat and cook included :) all the best!

author: Sam Allen
review_text: Amazing food, super friendly owner and staff. The salted coffee is one of the nicest things I've ever tasted. Highly recommended!

author: Laurent Bralé
review_text: Great spot for a delicious bánh mì. The food was fresh, flavourful, and well-balanced, and the service was friendly and efficient. Definitely worth a visit.

author: Ceiledh Monk
review_text: Lovely restaurant! Wanted to have bun cha one last time before flying out and this held up to my expectations. Lovely and welcoming staff too.

author: Kevin de Guzman
review_text:
Banh Mi Chao Dì Nu isn’t trying to be the best food in Vietnam and that’s exactly why it works. What it does offer is arguably the best bánh mì chảo you’ll find in the heart of District 1 (IMO) especially if you’re looking for something local, comforting, and honest.

The dish arrives sizzling in a small pan, packed with familiar favorites: eggs, sausage, pate, meat, and sauce bubbling together, meant to be scooped up with crusty bread. While it may not blow you away compared to legendary spots across Vietnam, within central D1, it stands out as a go to for a solid Banh mi chao fix.

The vibe is very much local eatery. You can sit outside on the street or head next door to the connected indoor space if you want shade.

author: xin
review_text: stumbled upon this local breakfast spot. not many tourists around and the seating is a bit limited and packed, but the food taste really delicious! worth coming if you’re nearby!!!!

author: Sim Hui Cheah
review_text: Found this better than usual banh mi, new experience unlocked- having breakfast on roadside ; baguette was too good crispy outside n soft inside , i had to take away , guess what its only 5k each for a plain baguette 😭😭😭

author: Yau Xue Yen
review_text:
Saw the recommendation on social media so we decided to visit after eating so much normal banh mi.

Surprisingly there wasn't a lot of customer, only locals. We ordered the special version (number 2) and it was soooo great 😭💕 too good that we visited twice hahaha

The owner doesn't know much English but we managed to communicate. The serving was fast and they are quite nice overall. We only tried the banh mi, but they do sell other dishes as well!

Five star from Malaysian ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐👍

author: Kenny King Yu Lau
review_text:
Banh Mi (Vietnamese bread)using McDonald all-day-breakfast concept,.

Bread was very crispy, dip with the sauce and it marches the meats.

No air conditioning, seating can be on the street which can be good to taste the Vietnamese style
Serve with very hot plate, just caution.

author: Simmie Wong
review_text: I think i like the pickle most. Apart from banh mi, this is also their traditional breakfast. Good to give it a try. It is a roadside stall and i arrived 830am on weekday. Not much people and no waiting time

author: J. H.
review_text:
Really lucky that this place was near my hotel but I’d have gladly made the journey here anyway.

It’s a tightly run ship here, the boss & staff are attentive and quick. Everything from getting seated, ordering, getting my food and paying the bill went smoothly. Appreciate them for kindly offering an extra chair, when they saw I rested my bag on my lap. You don’t have to worry about not speaking any Vietnamese. As things are quite fast paced, it wouldn’t hurt to check if the change you received is correct.

Clearly a favourite among foreigners and locals alike. A hearty way to start the day!

author: Julian Aguilar
review_text:
I had special Bánh mì chảo (beef, egg, sausage, cheese, meatball, ham and pate) and it was so good.

Price:

July 3 = 55k
July 4 = 57k
July 5 = 60k

Date: 5/7/25

author: Daniel Tee
review_text: I love Banh Mi and this Banh Mi Chao taste just absolutely phenomenal. Very authentic, very hearty, you really can't go wrong with this place.

author: Torn Marom
review_text: I ordered the Banh Mi Chao Upgrade, and it was very good with a taste different from a regular Banh Mi. I recommend trying it. The staff also provided good service.

author: Paing Soe Thu
review_text: I went there because of vlogger “what the pho” who shared about great foods in hochimin. It turned out i was scammed by the meal itself. The sausage and pate had odd smell, the baguette is cold and there were only little meat as you can see in the picture (normally 60k can get alot in other shops) Personally, i felt cheated and not worth the price at all. I feel disgusted “what the pho” because of her fake (paid partnership) content, they are not real reviews.

author: Ilene Dcosta
review_text:
Delicious Banh mi!!  Was so different to have it in this small table by the road but the taste was excellent. Very friendly owner, had a good variety of options
Also had the cold coffee. Would recommend for a hearty breakfast

author: Marianne Brabant
review_text: Great breakfast family restaurant in HCMC. Simple menu, not many options but they have mastered their dishes. The deconstructed banh mi is a must. All the fillings you’d usually have served in a flavourful broth with a side of fresh bread. Very filling, generous portion and fair priced the service is extremely fast.

author: Philipp Vater
review_text: My favourite breakfast spot in HCM. Very authentic place, great taste.

author: Macxchange Inc.
review_text: If you're looking for a good street side breakfast meal in Saigon, this is the place to be. Their baguette bread is to die for and perfect for Banh mi chao. The best!!!

author: Jasmine
review_text: I had the pleasure of trying banh mi chao for the first time, and it was absolutely divine! Even now that I'm back in my home country, I still find myself craving it. What made the experience even more special was the exceptional service from the gentleman serving us. He was kind, attentive, and ensured that we were enjoying our meal to the fullest. I'm looking forward to returning to Ho Chi Minh City and visiting this place again. Highly recommended!

author: Joseph Yiong (Joseph Yiong)
review_text: This is absolutely worth to try as it’s delicious. Especially like the half boiled egg with gravy.

author: Nicolai
review_text:
What can I say except what has already been said? The food is divine.

This is a no fuss, no muss dining experience where you’re in-and-out in 15 minutes: fuller, happier, and living a better life.

The staff in the narrow street will wave a welcoming hand towards their small collection of tables and stools, knowing that you’re already captive to the smell of sizzling eggs. Take a seat and stab your finger at the top of the page: banh mi chao special. Add a drink of choice and await the best little plate of breakfast in Vietnam.

Served piping hot, there’s a medley in the pan: eggs, lovely pork in various forms, pate, onions, laughing cow cheese (yes, that one), and fresh bread. There’s absolutely no wrong way to eat it! Haphazard chunks of bread with a sloppy spoonful of meats, the distant honking of passing cars, and the cool bittersweet taste of bac xiu coffee is the recipe for a great day.

Come once, come again, and eat your heart out.

author: Jay Carrillo
review_text: Amazing food, friendly people. Came 2 days in a row and got a special banh mi for lunch. It's one of the best banh mi choa's I've ever had and regular banh mi is best in the area. The homemade chilli paste is amazing, the bread is crusty and fresh, pate is tasty and I love the cheese - nice touch.

author: Hoang Ngan
review_text:
Great place to experience baguette with a combo pan. They have inside seats as well as outside seats. The food is served very fast and hot. The first one (mix option) is good enough for breakfast.
They also have free special butter which is usually served in Banh Mi food stalls.
I do not recommend the kumquat tea here, so tasteless.
Price: 45.000 - 60.000/ person

author: Sukha Lee
review_text:
The pho soup here is very clean and rich in flavor, not greasy at all but still deeply satisfying. You can really taste how well the broth is prepared, and it feels light while still being hearty. The coconut drink was sweet and refreshing, which paired really nicely with the meal.

I ordered the soup with a variety of meats, and everything was cooked perfectly. The ox tail stood out the most, it was tender, flavorful, and added a lot of depth to the broth. Overall, the restaurant is clean, the food tastes amazing, and you can tell a lot of care goes into each dish. I would definitely come back if I’m craving a comforting bowl of pho.

author: Trista
review_text:
We came here because it’s listed in the Michelin Guide. Pho Viet Nam has many branches, and this is the one mentioned in the list.

It is delicious. The noodles are homemade and have a great texture. I ordered the wagyu hot stone pho with mixed beef (oxtail, tendon, raw beef etc.), while my spouse chose the wagyu pho bò tái (raw beef only, no tendon). Both were excellent, and the broth was especially impressive: rich and deeply flavorful. There are sauces and pickles were ready on the table as well to adjust to our liking.
They also serve fried bread sticks for 20,000 VND (5 sticks), which pair nicely with the pho.

P.S.: I enjoyed it so much that I ended up going back again to another Pho Viet Nam branch that was closer to our stay (Sheraton area) and the quality and taste were very consistent, and for us it even felt like it came with larger portions of noodles.

author: Hayashi Rina (YT : cocofunnyoversea)
review_text:
I thought it would be difficult to get a seat, but it turned out their seating system is very smooth and fast.

The broth is the soul of the pho — so rich and comforting. The hot stone is a brilliant idea to keep the pho hot and makes it easy to cook the raw beef perfectly.

I ordered the beef ball + raw beef, and wow… those beef balls are so chewy and incredibly tasty!

Definitely worth a visit, and it has become one of my comfort foods in Ho Chi Minh City.

author: Steven W
review_text:
Went during middle of the day so was seated immediately. Found the place as it was really close by to our hotel and it was just okay. The broth itself had good flavour but nothing overly special. The one thing that was good was the fresh rice noodles.

For the price it is also on the more expensive side relative to other restaurants and pho places.

author: Joey Ngui
review_text:
It’s my second time eating this pho, and it was perfect after walking outside the whole day. At midnight, when I was on the way back to the hotel and feeling hungry, this warm bowl of pho was exactly what I needed. The soup was very, very good, and the beef was fresh. The raw beef is placed into the stone bowl after the food is served at the table, and it cooks just nicely, very tender and delicious.

I wanted to try the fried dough sticks too, but the portion was too big since I was eating alone, so I didn’t order it in the end. Hopefully they can offer a smaller portion option next time 😂

author: louise
review_text:
First — the bread they put on your table is not free. So if you think you won’t finish it, don’t open it lol it was also very crispy and it was nice to dip in the soup.

We got seated right away, we came at 8AM. We ordered and got our food within 5-10 minutes and it was flavourful.

Honest opinion– the broth is really good as well as the freshly made noodles, however, I think there are better pho restaurants than this one.

I wouldn’t come back but it was good to try the Michelin ⭐️⭐️⭐️ pho.

People generally stay around 30 minutes and would leave right away.

PS, they don’t have any high chairs for the babies, so prepare to have them on your lap if they can’t sit by themselves yet.

author: Raymond Lai
review_text:
Very much a tourist hotspot here. If you fancy a bowl that is "Michelin recommended", then I would make a visit.

There is better pho from local joints just a block away, but a pilgrimage here is worth it just to experience the hustle and bustle of a Michelin recommended joint.

Broth was good and clear, slightly sweet. Meat quantity was good. Noodles were softer that those from northern Vietnamese restaurants.

The place is PACKED with tourists, with Insta360s and GoPros everywhere. If you're looking for a locals only experience, it's best to check elsewhere.

author: Nomadicus
review_text:
Pho Viet Nam in Ho Chi Minh City is undeniably a destination spot, the kind of place travelers seek out because of its Michelin star rather than because a local nudged them there. I visited at the very start of my Vietnam trip, which ended up being helpful—I had a well-recognized version of pho to compare against everything else I tried along the way.

Service is quick and efficient, and the broth is clean, flavorful, and well crafted. But beyond that, not much else signaled a Michelin-level experience for me. It was good pho, but not transformative pho.

A couple of notes: the Chinese fried bread costs extra, and the stone hot pot option—while dramatic—is more gimmick than enhancement. Skip the theatrics and go for the simple bowl.

I’m glad I tried it, especially as a benchmark, but whatever magic the guide recognized didn’t quite translate to my visit. It's a solid stop, just not the standout I had hoped for.

author: Christopher Wu
review_text:
For Vietnam, I only had a few pho spots while here, but this one was definitely the benchmark — easily the best one I had. I wasn’t a fan of the hot stone pho though; I felt like the broth became too diluted, and there was a bit of a weird colouration to it that threw me off. The flavour of the meat also didn’t hit the mark for me.

The regular bowl, on the other hand, was packed with such a hearty broth. I ordered the beef pho — not a huge amount of meat inside, so if you’re someone who likes it loaded, I’d recommend adding extra beef. The noodles were as good as it gets, a bit on the thicker side but still held a nice bite.

Service here was also really solid — they seat you quickly and the food comes out fast. Overall, a comforting bowl and easily my favourite pho experience in Vietnam.

author: Igha Ayemi
review_text: Pho Vietnam was one of the highlights of my trip. The food was so good that I came back a second time. Impeccable hygiene, fast and organised staff, and outstanding flavours. Truly deserving of its Michelin recognition. A must visit!

author: Dea Proborini
review_text:
I was looking for a famous Pho restaurant near my Airbnb in HCMC and gladly found this Michelin Guide one.
My friend and I ordered Beef Shank Pho, Passion Fruit Juice, Mulberry Juice and Crispy Bread.
The Pho was served in a big bowl with some generous beef shank. The beef broth was very comforting and it really shooted my sore throat.
Get some herbs and chili sauce to your bowl and it goes much flavorful. Don't forget to dip the crispy bread into the broth, it adds a delightful chrunchy texture.
Overall, it is a simple yet heartwarming dish that feels perfect for a cozy meal!

author: Ashley T (Shark and Eagle)
review_text: It’s honestly pretty good, compare to other pho place, I wish they have special beef( combination of all type of meat like we do back in Melbourne). The price is reasonable with choices of sizes!! That’s really good because I just want small dishes.

author: Ramdas Prabhu
review_text: This Michelin star restaurant deserves their rating as the Pho is very delicious and one of the best I've had in Vietnam. Their juice items were also tasty. We tried the Beef shank and Beef rib pho..the Shank was very soft and juicy while the Ribmeat was a bit chewy. Must try the Mulberry juice and orange carrot juice. Shop is very clean and service quick and efficient.

author: 布鲁塞尔糯米糍
review_text:
I ordered the C2 hot-stone beef pho, which comes with raw beef slices and cooked beef brisket. On the side you get beef broth, scallions, bean sprouts, lemongrass, Thai basil, and fresh chili.
The taste is very close to the classic pho I’ve had before. The stone bowl arrives piping hot, so you can cook the raw beef yourself, almost like a mini hot pot. Don’t rush it the way I did—if you add all the beef at once, it clumps together. Take your time and swish the slices in the broth for the best texture.
The fresh chili is seriously spicy, so add with care. The chili sauce on the table packs heat too. The broth here is noticeably fresher and a touch sweeter than what I’ve had in Europe, and it tastes far less like MSG. European pho really does cut corners on slow-simmered stock.
Overall, this bowl beats any pho I’ve tried in Europe or Japan. I can’t compare it to local Vietnamese spots since this is the only one I’ve tried so far, but I’ll definitely explore more next time. The shop itself is small, clean, and welcoming, with plenty of foreign visitors. Both card and cash are accepted.

author: Sam Shee
review_text:
Best beef noodle broth bombardment, with a big boost of pungent raw meat and wet veggies as soon as you waltz in.

Lots of seating and great for groups if you don't mind having no space to put all these big bowls of slurpy flat noodles. Broth flavour is top notch and the beef is chunky and chewy like it should be.

There's two shops in close proximity so head on over to the overflow outlet. Staff speak workable English which is handy.

author: Peter Tan
review_text:
Don't be fooled by the small shop front, the narrow corridor retry leads to a rather sizable dining hall.

The pho taste nice and the wagyu beef is tender, one of the best pho that I have ever eaten. The soursop drink is basically blended soursop, that's why it taste so rich and yummy.

author: Manaschanok Buanark
review_text:
We absolutely love Pho Viet Nam!!!
This particular meal marked my very first time experiencing the authentic dish right here in Vietnam, and it was unforgettable. I was especially impressed by the soup, as I had ordered the hot pot style. The beautiful thing about the hot pot is that the broth remained consistently piping hot throughout, allowing me to cook the meat precisely to my preferred doneness—a perfect, personalized experience.

author: Ailin Goh
review_text:
Clearly I looked like a tourist!
But jokes aside, the service is excellent. I got a 1 on 1 lesson on how to eat my bowl of Pho. Pairing with the vege and sauce I need to dip my meat with. Food is good.
It was an easy 3mins walk from my hotel.  First meal when I landed. Thumbs up!  Will be back for sure.

author: Mihwa Lee
review_text:
Was busy even at 10am, but was seated immediately. Glad they offered small portions and even those without noodles for light eaters.
The small portion however was still quite substantial.
I had the raw beef pho. Found the beef not that thinly sliced and quite tough. Broth was very tasty and flavorful. Noodles were broad and soft. The fried dough was very nice after soaking up the soup.

author: An Le
review_text: First time at this famous spot and it lived up to the hype. The broth was amazing, with good noodles and beef. Appreciated the air-conditioned space, and the portion sizes were just right. Would come back.

restaurant: Mặn Mòi, Tao Đàn - 34 Võ Văn Tần
author: Adam Do
review_text:
We randomly came across this restaurant while walking around Saigon, and it ended up being one of the best meals we had during our trip. It’s clearly very popular and well known, there was a wait when we arrived.

The architecture and design of the restaurant are incredible and truly one of a kind. It reminded us of a Studio Ghibli–style aesthetic, with beautiful details throughout. The interior features Portuguese-style tiles on the floors, and as you move up each level, the space opens into different Studio Ghibli–inspired scenes. It’s an amazing place for photos as well as dining.

We ordered an entrée featuring dried mushrooms, broccolini, and lotus, which was incredible. We also had the sautéed garlic chive flowers with Sapa wild mushrooms, light, fresh, and full of flavour, the perfect refreshing dish.

For the main, we shared the salt-baked Man Hill pork platter, served with wild herbs and rice paper. It was outstanding. Wrapping the pork with herbs in rice paper made for the perfect bite, simple, balanced, and absolutely delicious.

The restaurant is busy, and we had to wait about 30 minutes, but it was well worth it. We just walked around the area and came back. Definitely recommend booking ahead if you can, this place is a must-visit in Saigon.

restaurant: Mặn Mòi, Tao Đàn - 34 Võ Văn Tần
author: choco cake
review_text:
Food was very delicious. This is probably one of the best meals we'e had throughout our whole stay in Vietnam. Menu was also easy to understand.

Staff were very accommodating and welcoming.

Place is very beautiful and almost every spot is picture perfect, even tbe bathroom and elevator.

Atmosphere is very warm and relaxing.

restaurant: Mặn Mòi, Tao Đàn - 34 Võ Văn Tần
author: Ghazal Lotfi
review_text:
Man Moi is a cute restaurant in Ho Chi Minh City. The building is beautiful and has a great design. The food was good, though a bit on the expensive side. We tried the anchovy salad, sticky rice with chicken and mushroom, and the sturgeon fish. Everything tasted great and we enjoyed all the dishes.

The general manager, Phuong, came by our table to check on us as well which was great.

The only downside was that there were no napkins on the table. Other than that, it was a good experience and we would recommend the restaurant.

restaurant: Mặn Mòi, Tao Đàn - 34 Võ Văn Tần
author: David Ha
review_text:
My first dinner on my 6th trip to Vietnam, and Man Moi was an absolute standout. Food was amazing—great portions, fair prices, and top-quality dishes. The nighttime ambiance is beautiful, and the service was excellent from start to finish.

Loved the chilled tea to start, and every dish impressed: roasted baby shrimp, beef jerky papaya salad, grilled frog sausage with veggies and rice paper, and the incredible two-way duck on a hot stone plate.

One of my best dining experiences in Ho Chi Minh City. Definitely a place I’ll revisit and my top recommendation for friends visiting

restaurant: Mặn Mòi, Tao Đàn - 34 Võ Văn Tần
author: SO
review_text:
The restaurant is truly architecturally beautiful, the building was very artistic, modern yet cultural at the same time. Absolutely loved the vibes. Service was also pretty great, staff were polite, friendly and also efficient.

The food however was a little disappointing. Bear in mind I did not order their signature dishes.

We’d order their chicken as appetiser and that was the only solid dish. The rest were a flop, imo. Shrimp friend rice was alright but nothing out of this world.

The baby shrimp was overly salty. Chives with mushroom dish was also just alright. The vegetable soup tasted fine but the odour of the veggie was very strong, while I was able to endure, I don’t think many others can.. The squid dish was the most disappointing, sauce was very good but the squid itself was really tough to chew on and there’s no QQ aspect to it.

I wanted to love Man Moi badly.
Most likely would not revisit again, unfortunately. Price was on the high side which I don’t mind but the food was really mediocre.

restaurant: Mặn Mòi, Tao Đàn - 34 Võ Văn Tần
author: Steve Chan
review_text:
A very beautiful setting for lunch or dinner.  We booked a table online for dinner, and it was very convenient.   The entire place is full of surprises and is great for taking photos.  The service was excellent from the time you get off the car to your table.
The only disappointment is the food is not as great as I expected.  However, the presentation of the food was excellent.  Again great for photos.  We ordered grilled chicken and duck breast, they were both either overcooked or dry / tough.  Overall, it is still a great place to spend an evening.

restaurant: Mặn Mòi, Tao Đàn - 34 Võ Văn Tần
author: Fritz
review_text:
I recently had the pleasure of visiting Mà Mới, a Vietnamese restaurant in Ho Chi Minh City, and it definitely lived up to the hype! If you’re a fan of authentic Vietnamese cuisine, this place is a must-try.

The vibe of the restaurant was super chill—casual yet stylish. It’s a great spot if you’re hanging out with friends or even having a relaxed meal by yourself. The staff was friendly and welcoming, which made the experience even better.

Now, the food. Oh wow. I started with their pho, and it was everything I hoped for. The broth was rich and flavorful, and the meat was tender—just the right balance of spices. I also tried their banh xeo (Vietnamese pancakes), which were crispy on the outside and packed with savory fillings. Honestly, I could eat those all day. For dessert, I went with che ba mau (three-color dessert), and it was a refreshing sweet ending to the meal.

The prices were pretty reasonable for the quality of food you get, and the portions were generous. If you’re craving authentic Vietnamese dishes that hit the spot, Mà Mới definitely delivers.

Overall, I had a fantastic time, and I’m already planning my next visit. Highly recommend it if you’re in Ho Chi Minh City and want to taste some amazing local flavors!

restaurant: Mặn Mòi, Tao Đàn - 34 Võ Văn Tần
author: Catherine Huynh
review_text: Such a dissopointment. Booked a table 2 days in advance and was excited for it as reviews were good. Architecture is immaculate but it doesnt compensate for the food. Spring rolls were decent but the veggies with it meh. Farm chicken hot pot was disastrous, we didnt enjoy it at all. Practically no chicken, only veggies and rice noodles. High prices so expected a lot more than this. Craft beers were the only good thing. Service couldve been more attentive at a place like this, got better service in pizza 4p.

restaurant: Mặn Mòi, Tao Đàn - 34 Võ Văn Tần
author: Mustafa Yehia
review_text:
Most people can’t even decide on a tie, and here they are handing you two menus and expecting you to behave. It’s an embarrassment of riches, really—Mặn Mòi and Hum Lounge playing house in a garden that’s far more tranquil than my last three massages.
Here is how you handle a table for three without looking like an amateur:
The Nem Vuông Nấm: These mushroom squares are a miracle of engineering. Usually, "plant-based" is just a polite way of saying "we ran out of ideas," but these are crispy, golden little boxes of secrets. They have more personality than most people I've worked with.
The "Wrapped Meat" Ritual: Whether it’s the Gà nướng lá dứa (Pandan Chicken) or the Bò nướng ống tre (Beef in Bamboo), it’s dinner as a DIY project. You wrap the meat, you commit to the flavor, and you pretend you’ve done something productive with your hands. It’s smoky, tender, and—since we’re skipping the pork—tactically brilliant.
The Cơm Chiên Gà Đồng, Lá É: Fried rice with lemon basil. It smells better than a French perfume and actually delivers on the promise. It’s the kind of starch that doesn't just sit there; it performs.
The Dừa Nướng: They grill the coconut because, apparently, just being a fruit wasn’t dramatic enough. It’s chilled, it’s sweet, and it’s the only thing in this humidity that actually works as advertised.
The Verdict: We skipped the pork and I didn't feel a hint of deprivation. Sit in the garden, order with the confidence of a man with a gold card, and let everyone think you’re a genius. It’s much easier than actually being one.

restaurant: Mặn Mòi, Tao Đàn - 34 Võ Văn Tần
author: Mai
review_text:
We visited Mặn Mòi, Tao Đàn while traveling through Vietnam and happened to be in Ho Chi Minh City for a friend’s birthday. The reservation process was really smooth and friendly — we even received a nice confirmation by email, which we appreciated.

The food was delicious, and the atmosphere felt warm and inviting. The restaurant itself is beautifully designed, and we also liked the little shop on the ground floor.

After dinner, we had a short and very nice chat with the General Manager Phuong Vu, which made the evening feel even more personal. Definitely a lovely spot for great food in the heart of the city.

restaurant: Mặn Mòi, Tao Đàn - 34 Võ Văn Tần
author: laura korwa
review_text: Had lunch here today and it was one of the most delicious meals I’ve had during my Saigon trip. Ordered the two-style duck breast, grilled pork, and shrimp rolls all fresh, flavorful, and beautifully served. The place feels cozy and green, with a relaxing scent and unique design. Staff were kind, attentive, and gave honest advice on portions; rare and much appreciated. A refreshing, high-quality dining spot. Definitely recommend!

restaurant: Mặn Mòi, Tao Đàn - 34 Võ Văn Tần
author: Lenard Sison
review_text: Best meal of my life. The pork jowl, eel sausage, chicken pandan, and baked coconut (drink) were immaculate. Actually had to run back the drink FOUR TIMES. This restaurant was our first meal, and we absolutely had to make it our last as well. The staff, Trung (manager), Dung, and Tien were very accommodating. I cannot emphasize my love for this restaurant, I implore you to try it for yourself.

restaurant: Mặn Mòi, Tao Đàn - 34 Võ Văn Tần
author: Mindy Wong
review_text:
The restaurant is on the second and third floor, the first floor is a souvenir shop and has so many things worth buying. Definitely worth a visit, the staff were friendly and the place is really nice. The food was FANTASTIC, I would eat it again. The squid was the highlight for me.

Do your research before you order your food, the food I’ve ordered were delicious but I’ve seen people slandering the restaurant when they didn’t order the right things.

restaurant: Mặn Mòi, Tao Đàn - 34 Võ Văn Tần
author: Mia Malgioglio
review_text:
We sat in the Vegetarian floor. Good food and nice place to sit. Would have loved if all plates were hot when served, would have made a huge difference.
Overall nice experience to try, but not as flavourous as more traditional, cheap viet restaurants

restaurant: Mặn Mòi, Tao Đàn - 34 Võ Văn Tần
author: Joselyn Lim
review_text:
Excellent food, service is ok for they forget to serve us our veggies. We follow up on it then they apologize. Good conduct. At least they apologize. And they did not charge us the veggie.
We ordered the 2 styled duck which i love it so much.
The crab soup has a special taste which is so delicious also.
Squid with lime is also excellent.
Thumps up!!!
Hope you can keep up with your good service, good foods!!!

restaurant: Mặn Mòi, Tao Đàn - 34 Võ Văn Tần
author: ani jensen
review_text:
This place is magical! I stumbled upon it before I went to the war museum, and it was definitely a high end restaurant! I spent about 40 AUD which is a lot more than a street meal, but the experience was so fun and good to treat yourself.
They greeted me so nice and took care of everything for me. Hand towel, clearing my table and getting food to me so beautifully. The food was delicious!! Try the pork skewers, my fav. An amazing vibe and atmosphere while visiting sai gon.

restaurant: Mặn Mòi, Tao Đàn - 34 Võ Văn Tần
author: Wendy C
review_text:
WORST EXPERIENCE EVER! FOOD POISONED... STILL AT HOSPITAL...
I had dinner here on the 27th with my entire family of four. We were very excited to try this Michelin-recognized restaurant, but unfortunately the experience that followed was extremely distressing.

About three hours after dinner, I began experiencing severe vomiting and diarrhea, followed by intense abdominal pain. The pain became so overwhelming that I was unable to stand or lie down, I will rolling on the floor in pain and had to be taken to urgent care. At the hospital, I received multiple IV infusions for pain management, fever, and dehydration. Blood tests tested positive of infection, and I was diagnosed with A09 – infectious gastroenteritis and colitis (unspecified). I was given antibiotics and am still completing the course today. The hospital visit cost approximately $500 USD.

The following day, my brother and father developed the same symptoms—fever, vomiting, and diarrhea—and both required hospital treatment as well. As of today, my father is still experiencing a low-grade fever.

I want to keep this review as objective as possible. The restaurant itself is beautifully designed, and the shop on the first floor is charming—we spent around $450 there buying a lot of crafts. The food was good, though given the reputation and hype, we were expecting more.

Notably, the only member of our family who did not become ill was my mother. The only dish she did not eat was the crab hot pot.

When the hot pot was brought to our table, it was not boiling. After waiting for some time, we asked the waitress for assistance three separate times. The first time, we were told to wait a few more minutes. The second time, we were told that the soup had already been boiled in the kitchen and was safe to eat. Coming from another Asian country, my understanding is that hot pot should remain actively boiling while cooking raw ingredients to ensure food safety. We were reassured that this was the traditional way to eat it and that it would be fine.
Eventually, the staff portioned the soup and cooked the meat and vegetables for us in the pot, which was still not boiling. Trusting their guidance, we ate the dish. My mother chose not to eat anything from the hot pot, and she was the only one who did not fall ill.

I cannot say with certainty what specific pathogen caused our illness. However, three out of four people becoming seriously sick within hours of the same meal is deeply concerning. While local diners may be accustomed to certain practices, a restaurant of this caliber—especially one frequented by international guests—should take extra care with food safety and preparation standards. This was an extremely painful and costly experience for my family, and I hope this feedback is taken seriously!!!

restaurant: Mặn Mòi, Tao Đàn - 34 Võ Văn Tần
author: Melvin Lim
review_text: First time visit with friends. Staff very friendly we wait for our table 20minutes. So we at ground floor shopping buy some sourvenier than went up to 3rd floor for our dinner. Surprise us the food was so good. Try urself you will know. Will visit next round to call other choice. Staff recommend us the food as the picture show.

restaurant: Mặn Mòi, Tao Đàn - 34 Võ Văn Tần
author: Robyn Elliott
review_text: I was recommended by my hotel, La Passion Hotel Saigon, and it was sooo good I went back on a second day for lunch. My server, Ms Truc, was really helpful and her food recommendations greatly appreciated and extremely delicious. It's a beautiful decorated building, over 3 floors with elevator, with a shop on the ground floor paying homage to local Vietnamese products. I would have returned for dinner but this little gem is very solidly booked.  I'd recommend reserving a table in advance,  it'll be worth the planning. My compliments to the staff and the very attentive duty manager who made my dining experience so enjoyable,  thank you.

restaurant: Mặn Mòi, Tao Đàn - 34 Võ Văn Tần
author: Liên Trần
review_text: We went mainly for the architectural design and atmosphere and it didn't disappoint. The service is 10/10! The food wasn't the highlight though for what we'd expect at the higher price point, but still decent. The pork jowl was good but I forgot to take a photo. The "Homeland brew" was definitely what they decribe as "taste of memory" for me growing up drinking homemade "sâm mía lau" and the like.

author: Wee Loon Chia
review_text:
Followed the Michelin guide to this restaurant for some “home cooked” Vietnamese food. It has three floors each tastefully decorated with excellent vibes. Service was attentive. Claypot snakehead fish was succulent, mango chicken feet salad was good as well but the chicken feet was a little rough to bite, little pancakes with shrimps were delicious. Spring rolls with beef were ok. The sauces that come with the dishes were excellent and elevated the taste.

Overall I would recommend this restaurant.

author: Gregory Rack
review_text:
Nhà Tú earns its Michelin Bib Gourmand reputation.

What impressed me most was the precision of flavor: bright acidity, clean herbs, and deep savory notes without anything feeling heavy or muddy. Each dish tasted intentional—balanced, layered, and very “Vietnamese home cooking,” just sharpened.

We did have a small hiccup (the fish didn’t arrive as ordered), but it barely mattered because:
• the rest of the table was excellent (crispy bites, a vibrant salad, perfectly garlicky greens, and those shrimp bites were addictive)
• the owner handled everything with genuine warmth and professionalism

Cozy room, calm service, and food that feels both comforting and elevated. I’d come back without hesitation.

author: YMC
review_text:
Stopped in at Nhà Tư for dinner and everything felt like true home-style Vietnamese cooking. We had the sour fish soup with pineapple and tomatoes — bright, comforting, and perfectly balanced. The stir-fried vegetables were simple but really well done, still crisp with just the right amount of garlic. The clay-pot dish came out bubbling hot and packed with flavor, the kind of dish that makes you want to eat every last bite of rice with the sauce.

I also tried their house drink topped with an edible flower — refreshing, light, and a great match for the food. Cozy space, relaxed pace, and dishes that feel like they came straight from someone’s family kitchen. I’d definitely come back.

author: Shmiley C
review_text:
Date of visit: June 2025
English menu available.

Nha Tu is recognized with a Bib Gourmand by Michelin. I was able to find the location pretty easily. The place is small and does not have much seating. I was here around 2 PM, so maybe the lunch rush was done. There was no wait for a table for two.

I may have been judged for ordering too much food:
Cha gio (fried spring rolls) 88k VND - good, would recommend
Lau hua sua (oyster hot pot) 495k VND - I wish this dish came out earlier. It came out too late. Good to try!
Ca loc kho to (braised snakehead fish) 85k VND - eh, I wouldn't order this again.
Nac dam nuong mat ong (grilled pork w honey sauce) 105k VND - This dish was ok.
Cuon nem nuong (pork spring roll) 25k VND - I wouldn't get this again either. Ok to try.

Drinks were ok.
Guava juice 50k VND
Beer 39k VND

They do have Wifi. Need to ask for password.
Toilet is upstairs. Be careful the stairs are steep and no railing.
Credit card/tap accepted.
Service is meh.

author: Ko Sing Chin
review_text:
The cozy, warm atmosphere and vintage decor made for a truly authentic and peaceful dining experience.  Suitable for anyone looking for a relaxed, traditional Vietnamese vibe.
Highly recommend to try the braised snakehead fish dish. The fish was tender and flaky, absorbing the rich flavors of the sauce completely. The pork belly pieces added a nice textural contrast and richness to the dish.

author: Heizhudaddy
review_text:
Great food and service overall. Walked in early without a reservation and got a seat as long as we finish before 8pm. Glad we made it as the dishes were mostly superb.

Ordered the snails (5/5), hand roll platter(3.5/5), banh xeo (4/5), prawn sashimi (5/5) and pig’s stomach (4/5).

Will definitely be back again when I’m in HCMC in future.

author: George Mulang Chen
review_text: Very multi storey vietnamese restaurant tucked away in a backstreet. The shop front is lush with an inviting vibe. Inside the shop is thoughtfully decorated with intricate lighting and display objects. The food was quite nice. We ordered a hot pot style soup, a local alcoholic beverage, amongst other things. It was delicious.

author: Matas Daunys
review_text:
We absolutely loved this place. The stir-fried NZ mussels were incredible (just look at their size!), and the oyster hotpot with beef was soooo good - rich, comforting, and full of flavour. Portions are generous, seasoning is spot-on, and the whole experience felt warm and homely.

The cozy atmosphere and friendly service make it easy to see why they earned their Michelin Bib Gourmand status - definitely well-deserved.

One small note: take the reviews (mine included!) with a grain of salt, as they offer complimentary homemade grass jelly with coconut milk if you leave a review on TripAdvisor or Google Maps. Still, even without that, this place stands firmly at 5 stars.

author: John Guo
review_text:
Good authentic Vietnamese cuisine. The place has Michelin bib gourmand sign so is always busy and needs prior booking.

Tu - the owner is often there and very friendly. You can tell she really puts her heart into making the food. Really love the baby clam and the beef & oyster hotpot in coconut water

author: Ker Sin Wong
review_text:
Came back for 2nd visit, love the banh khot. First time trying steam stuffed snail which is exceptionally good. The Nha Tu beef salad was amazing as well.

Will definitely come back whenever I’m at HCMC!

author: Cedric Cha
review_text: Vietnamese food with a homecooked feel. Food is considerably cheap for a restaurant but portions are on the smaller side. Staff were friendly and helpful and the restaurant was cozy.

author: K Hochiminh
review_text:
This is a very delicious Vietnamese restaurant.
The location is difficult to find and the surrounding area is very congested, so access is not good, but the restaurant is always crowded with customers.
The food is also delicious, especially the shellfish stuffed with minced meat.
The specialty of this restaurant is hot pot.
We had chicken hot pot this time, but it was a bit disappointing as it contained spicy leaves and the chicken was very bony.
The oyster and pork hot pot I had previously was more delicious.
However, since I can't eat oysters, I think it would be even better if they had a hot pot with just pork.
The food is very delicious and reasonably priced, so I recommend this restaurant.

author: Rui Min Soh
review_text: Prices are relatively steeper for the portion but the quality was great. Good use of different flavours for the sauces. Banh xeo was awesome.

author: Scarlett Sum Yee Yeung
review_text: First time in Vietnam! Google recommended a place called Nha Tu, so my boyfriend and I decided to try their hotpot. After eating all the must-try Vietnamese dishes these past few days, we wanted something different. The hotpot with egg, oyster, and sliced beef was surprisingly delicious! They have most of the Vietname must eat food in the menu also.

author: Fiona
review_text: Incredible Vietnamese food. Best I’ve ever had. Comfortable, organic, vibrant, culturally relevant atmosphere. The server was extremely thoughtful, the best service I have ever received in a restaurant. I’m extremely impressed and Ill be back! 😍

author: Zie Rose
review_text: Worth for a try! The oyster is very fresh and the soup of the hot pot is very tasty! The staff here are very nice and friendly. Definitely would recommend those who travelling in Ho Chi Minh City!

author: Phuong Le
review_text: We had a great dinner at Nhà Tú! The food was flavorful, especially the oyster hotpot, which my boyfriend (who’s not usually into Vietnamese food or seafood) really enjoyed. The bánh xèo and grilled lemongrass beef were also delicious. Friendly and attentive service made the whole experience even better.

author: monica xian
review_text:
Great food. Just took a bit long to get to us.
Slightly pricey but worth it ! Love the hotpot. Natural flavours.

author: Eren Baştuğ
review_text: We ordered michellin recommended foods. Seafood omlette was delicious but fried rice was just okay, nothing special. Ambient and service is good.

author: E S
review_text:
AUGUST 2025. LOOK AT THE FOOD OMG THE PRESENTATION IS LOL

Tourist here. Very disappointed at service (expect to wAit 1.5hours) , they forget orders , and the food was extremely disappointing. Not sure why this place has michelin guide ? Food presentation is lacklustre.  DONT WASTE UR CALORIES HERE

author: Kenzie Winther
review_text: I went here three times. Twice in the same day. It was my first banh mi and my last of the trip. First off. They are cheap, big, and they don’t skimp. Every time I got the traditional number one with the cold cuts, veggies, liver pate etc. I loved every single bite. The bread is so fresh not matter the time of day you go. It was the best banh mi I had in all of Vietnam. You can eat on the curb or carry out. We did both. They are kind and patient. This was by far my favorite food experience while in Vietnam. Don’t miss it!

author: David Ho
review_text:
Great food, sitting on low chairs watching traffic and people go by. We had the roast pork banh mi, the banh bao and 2 iced coffees - all were great and would be one of our goto banh mi spots.

Servings can be quite large so if you’re extra hungry, get 2 of the large ones or split one large or 2 small.

author: Angela Killian
review_text:
Service was fast…food was ok, but not great vegetarian options. I got the vegetarian banh mi thinking it would be all veggies and it was all noodles and tofu with no sauce. I ordered again the omelette banh mi and it was really tasty. They want to get you in and out due to limited seating. Beer was ICE cold!

I think this place has a lot of hype from foreigners leaving reviews. It was good but not the best and they didn’t add any mayo which is a deal breaker for me personally.

author: SD
review_text:
This was my first time having Bánh Mi and I enjoyed it!

I had the mixed meat combo as that was recommended. The bread was super crisp and flaky with a decent amount of meat inside. If you’re not a lover of pate/sausage then I’d try something else on the menu.

Taste wise, the only thing that was lacking for me were the pickles, it needed the tangy sourness to bring it all together.

The mango smoothie was thick, sweet and refreshing, perfect for the humid climate.

I’d definitely go back if I have time to try the roast pork Bánh Mi as I think it’d be more up my street.

Note: this is more of a takeaway spot but there are a couple of deck chairs and small tables out front

author: Chuck Lee
review_text:
In the last day of my trip in Ho chi min city, I enjoyed breakfast in Banh Mi Hong Hoa restaurant with my wife.

The food is so gooooooooooood. I wish I tried earlier. Price is affordable, and staff is super friendly with a big smile on face.

Highly recommended to you guys.

author: Steven W
review_text:
Right around the corner from the other famous banh mi spot. This place was really good, it came filled with lots of meat and veggies. I wish I got the smaller size as we thought it would mot have been that big.

If you want to avoid the long lines and have a similar tier banh mi this place is on par.

author: Ray Sim
review_text:
My food rating guide:
2.5/5 ‐-------> Average taste
5/5 ‐--------> Scrumptious! (My comfort food! 🤩)

Very crispy and airy baguette. The BBQ pork (Banh Mi Thit Nuong) was flavourful and savoury. Not too sweet. Similar to 肉干 taste. The vege and herb were fresh and fragrant. Added egg that gave another layer of texture to it and enhanced the overall taste.

The chicken ( Banh Mi Sot Ga) was ok.

Dine at the low stools and table by a minor road watching grassroots activities was chill and had the locally-connected vibe.

The Banh Mi was a 4.7/5

author: Wendy
review_text:
Super good banh mi. The classic combo (No.1 on the menu) is my favorite. BBQ pork is a close second. The price between 45,000-55,000 is the size. If you don’t mention that you want small, the staff might just decide the big one for you. (That is what happened to us when we visited the first time.) *I think by big or small is the amount of meat, not bread size.

Before we left Vietnam, we went there 6am and they are already opened. There was a lady who was packing the bread. She looks like the owner of the place, she is super friendly and helpful. I absolutely love this place, will come back for more next time.

author: Chlotus
review_text: You can just tell from the outside that this place serves amazing food! The sandwich, Banh Mi, is absolutely delicious, especially with the meat. It may not be the classic flavor you expect, but I really enjoy it! I honestly think it's one of the best I’ve ever had.

author: Viet Nguyen
review_text: We discovered this place after trying a few banh mi joints around, including the famous Banh Mi Ba Huynh. This place has a wider selection and their banh mi is better IMO. 45K for the a normal size banh mi to $55K for the larger size. Hands down its the best banh mi I've had so far. Definitely worth trying if you havent yet.

author: Lorraine Bmor
review_text:
The other more famous shop has more queues over Bánh Mì Hồng Hoa, and is generally the popular spot for tourists, but don’t let fool you. Bánh Mì Hồng Hoa is far superior (atleast for me) and here is why:

1. Size:
Bigger isn’t always better. 🙈 The competitor offers just one massive size of banh mi while Hong Hoa gives you an option; one that is as big as the rival shop and one that is just the right size that’ll give you the perfect bite with everything in it (bread, veggies, and meat). Since the competitor’s is so big, it’s impossible to get that perfect bite, unless of course, you have an equally as massive mouth. Lol.

2. Variety:
The other shop has only one Banh Mi option which is the traditional “put every Vietnamese charcuterie” in a baguette. It’s tasty and the most traditional but you’d get tired of it easily. More options would be better. Meanwhile, Hong Hoa has 6 varieties to choose from with their Bread with Roast Pork option being the best!

3. Price:
The other shop’s pricing, as mentioned by many, is too expensive at 73K VND. Yes, it is big. But Hong Hoa offers the same size at just 55K VND.  🤷🏻‍♀️

4. Taste:
Not gonna lie, the rival’s is delicious as heck but there is a thing as over filling. It has too much meat, butter, and paté that it has become too overwhelming on the taste buds. They give you separate packs of fresh greens and pickled vegetables but even that isn’t enough to balance out the flavors.

On the other hand, Hong Hoa’s is perfectly balanced. We tried both their Roast Pork and Mixed Meat one which is similar to Huynh Hoa’s to give it a fair comparison.

For the Mixed Meat one, the slices of ham and paté taste better here although not as generous and the other shop. Again, Quality > Quantity. 😉 And for the Roast Pork one, it is hands down the best Banh Mi I’ve had in my life!!!!! The pork is nicely charred and its fattines goes really well with the pickled veggies. It meat is kinda reminiscent of Pork Sisig (a Filipino dish). It even has that spicy little kick from the chilies. It’s a sandwich worth the trip back to Saigon! 💯

Either way, both these Saigon banh mi shops made the most famous stall (for tourists) in Hanoi, Banh Mi 25, taste like utter crap. Lol. 🤣

author: Mark T
review_text: Good alternative to Huynh Hoa that’s just around the corner. Larger menu so more options than Huynh Hoa - we ordered roast pork which was delicious. There was no pate/sauce so it could’ve done with a bit more flavour. There’s also seating for about 10 people out the front if you’re dining in.

author: Lyza P
review_text:
July 2025 visit

This was recommended to me in 2023 by our tour guide, and I forgot the flavor he suggested.
So, my cousin and I ordered "EXTRA MIXED MEATS," which was a disaster - it had I think some sort of Liver spread or taste? Which I do not eat.

Should've stuck with pork BBQ or roast pork and read the reviews instead of going to the top order. Kind of ruined the Bahn Mi experience for both of us.

Atmosphere is great though and there weren't a lot of people at 9 AM.

author: Rick Takeshita
review_text: More balanced than the other famous one around the corner 😜 plus they have thin, lighter, crisper bread. Outside seated Vietnam vibes n no wait.

author: Josephine Ruth
review_text:
The ban minh is good. Flavourful. Ordered the BBQ pork and Roast pork. The bread is abit hard for me but this is just my preference.
My friends find it just right.

author: Pragyan Bezbaruah
review_text: Better than Huynh Hoa - for sure. More food options. The roasted pork was delicious. The sad thing however is that the Dac Biet, which is supposed to be special Bánh Mì, felt empty. Yes, meat was in abundance but no eggs given. Have had better ones on the streets - everything in abundance and still will charge 40k. Hong Hoa charged us 55k.

author: Lift_Run_Eat_
review_text: The better of the two in area (Huynh being the other). The filling is what stands out here, I went for the bbq pork and it was excellent (nice bits of crackling in there and mixed cuts). I also had the pork balls one and that was also excellent. I’d happily try any of the others on the menu with confidence. The extras (bao & wrapped leave bao) were very average, far too much bun and not enough filling. Stick to the Banh Mi and you can’t go wrong!

author: Anny Phan
review_text: so good! i ordered the #1 special and it was so filling, it's actually quite a large banh mi so if you don't eat that much i'd suggest sharing it with someone

author: Liz Gallibult
review_text: Ordered a roasted pork banh mi with pickles, chillies, and no cilantro for VND 45.000 and it’s quite worth the hype. Pork tasted amazing with crispy skin and slightly salted pungent roasted flavor. However, due to the 50:50 proportion of meat and veggies, the banh mi eventually turned out a little bit bland for me. Big portion, gotta take the other half away home.

author: Ed Hsiung
review_text:
Bread baked fresh....Best of all Banh Mi. Street side seating so subject to fumes from motorbikes and the staff are what you expect....crude and to the point.
Worth to visit at least once...maybe twice. Haha!

author: Eric Nguyen
review_text:
Banh Canh Cua 87 delivers standout crab udon with a broth that’s rich, clean, and unmistakably crab forward. The noodles have great bite, the crab meat is fresh and plentiful, and the flavors cut through with real precision. From a product standpoint, it outperforms a lot of more commercial spots.

Atmosphere is a 3 minimal, functional, and clearly designed for quick turnover. Service is a 3 – fast, direct, and very “sit, eat, and go,” which fits the local street-shop operating model but isn’t meant to be leisurely.

Even with the stripped down setup, the food quality carries the experience. If you want premium banh canh cua without the noise or the gimmicks, this shop remains a high value, repeat worthy choice.

author: Mi Phan
review_text: The broth is rich and flavorful, with generous toppings like fresh crab, shrimp, and thick tapioca noodles. The place is simple and often busy, but the quality and value are outstanding. A great spot for real local food.

author: Ming Shen Tham
review_text:
Honestly, I never expected it to be this good. The broth was rich and packed with intense crab and prawn flavour, the kind that immediately makes you want to slurp up the whole bowl.
There were also bits of real crab meat in the soup, which added authenticity and texture. The only downside was the occasional pieces of cartilage, which made eating it a little annoying at times.
At around 60,000 VND per bowl, it’s extremely worth the price, especially considering the flavour and portion.
The place itself is cramped, and you will have to sit on low stools in a tight space, but honestly, the food and value make it completely worth it.

author: Meagan
review_text:
As a tourist, this is the best local/street food meal I’ve had in Saigon so far. I’m not the biggest fan of seafood, which says a a-lot.

Broth has a medium-thick consistency and all the seafood is fresh. Very delicious & affordable!

author: Ray Sim
review_text:
My food rating guide:
2.5/5 ‐-------> Average taste
5/5 ‐--------> Scrumptious! (My comfort food! 🤩)

Light gooey savoury sauce. Smooth and soft silver needle noodle/老鼠粉/bee tai bak. Came with prawn, quail eggs, crab meat, crab meat cake (I think), blood cake, and sliced pork.

The suace might look thick but it was like soup. Satisfying.

The bowl of noodle was a 4.2/5

author: Eric Hia
review_text:
The stall has their combination of bahn cahn. Dish soup has a slight gooey texture. Fish cake was made from river fish flesh hence has a soil taste.

Relatively small space with very low tables and chairs.

Been there, dined it. May return.

author: Jasmine (Jas.eats)
review_text:
ORDERED:
🍜 01 Phần: 55,000 đ
🍩 Bánh Quẩy: 3,000 đ

REVIEW:
❤️ Delicious food.
1 option means this is definitely a specialty store.
I also adore soup that isn't too gelatinous (I prefer mine more watery), a strong taste from the sweetness of the crab, decked full of flavour.
Genuinely delicious and would go back.

Dipping the fried doughnuts into the soup at the end softened the crispy batter. It's a fun way to end the meal as well.

Service is straight forward, and you might share a table with strangers. It's not as compressed as Hong Kong, so I was alright.

author: Nguyen-An Dang
review_text: very good. excellent. speedy service. food was delish. add some lime to allow the flavors to enhance. was in n out in under 10mins. 58,000 dong. solid price. has additional options for more protein, etc.

author: Anna Koh
review_text: delicious food! each portion came with pork slices, crab meat, crab fishcake and blood cake. generous serving for the price paid. worth a try!

author: Kelyn Ngui
review_text: Low chair seating. Small space for small groups. The taste is flavourful with prawn crab pork and quail egg, also have pig blood

author: Kaylee Nguyen
review_text:
I really love this place! 🍜 The soup is flavorful, and the toppings are fresh. Conveniently located in District 1, it’s not far from many popular tourist spots, making it easy to stop by and try. 55k vnd/ bowl

Tip: Visit around lunch after 11am or 5–6 PM (close at 9pm) to avoid the crowds.

author: Ashley Lo
review_text: One of my favourite meals of my trip! It was a bit of a distance from where I was staying (which was D1) but totally worth it! I took a 25 minute bike ride during peak hour all the way there and it was really worth it. The crab broth is so rich and yummy, with so many ingredients in there. However, the youtiao was not crispy and pretty cold though, so will recommend you to ask them to heat it up if possible - I didn’t as I arrived close to their closing time so I didn’t want to trouble them. Service is really quick and you’ll be seated at low stools which made the experience quite enjoyable as I felt like a local there enjoying my meal. I also ordered a chrysanthemum drink which paired really well with the heartiness of the broth. Really good meal, something different from the usual Vietnamese fare. Will definitely be back next time I’m in Saigon!

author: Clay
review_text:
Wouldn't have known this dish exists, if I didn't come to vietnam. Not as popular as banh mi or pho outside of vietnam, but definitely worth to try if you're here!

The chili is pure fire.

So so good. Would come back again someday!

author: Neil Nicholas
review_text:
Food and broth is so yummy! Be careful as the grind chillies are a bomb but should add some to elevate the broth!

Can when they just open at 11am and if you can’t seat low chairs beware yea.

author: Alex Pham
review_text: Not my taste though. Maybe I prefer bánh canh with more broth. The crab was okay. The wet tissue was quite strange, it had liquid inside, and when I opened it, all the liquid spilled onto me.

author: PAUL
review_text:
· A must-try bánh canh! The crab and prawn noodles are incredible. Never disappoints!
· Unforgettable bánh canh cua. Huge prawns, rich broth, and you MUST get the quẩy!
· The best bánh canh cua! Full of seafood, delicious broth, and great price.
· 100% recommend. A delicious, hearty bowl of noodles that always hits the spot.
· A legendary bowl of noodles! The broth is so rich and flavorful, packed with crab meat and a giant prawn. Absolutely must eat it with the quẩy (fried breadstick) for the full experience. Amazing value.
· You haven't had bánh canh until you've tried here. The seafood is fresh and generous. The price is fair for the huge, delicious bowl. Don't forget to order quẩy to dip in the soup!
· My favorite comfort food. The broth is perfection, the seafood is plentiful, and it's always consistent. A true Hanoi classic. Pro tip: always get extra quẩy!

author: No Cool
review_text: Delicious and authentic Vietnamese crab noodle soup. However, the map shows the place is a bit tricky hopefully you can find it :).

author: Rae Zyon
review_text: I love their crab noodles, the soup is thick and rich, it's very flavourful and well seasoned. The noodles are smooth and silky. Plenty of toppings and comes with a side of dough sticks that elevates this experience even more.

author: TAY AARON
review_text: Food was amazing. Thick and nice! No need for words just point to the picture and say how many bowls you want. Let the food do the talking! Highly recommended. Definetely a 5star!

author: Meng Cheakorng
review_text: The food is very tasty, u can taste the crab meat and the broth also taste like crab soup

author: lim jenn ching
review_text:
I order beef combination pho, it doesnt comes with medium size, the rest of the choice does.
Pho was decent it was tasteful meat is tender, beef ball bouncy tendon was succulent beef tripe was crunchy. It was happiness in one big bowl.
During my visit it was packed so be prepare to wsit for them to attend to you.
Overall i think for a good bowl of pho it was worth the wait.
Oh yah there will be line too if its nearer to lunch time.

author: Anika Patil
review_text: Dropped by Pho Hoa Pasteur on Pasteur Street and had their beef pho. The broth was rich and fragrant, with a nice balance of flavors — deep but clean. The beef cuts and noodles felt fresh and generous. Good value for the price  definitely worth checking out if you want a solid bowl of pho in Saigon.

author: Lawrence Lau
review_text: My second visit! The pho was amazing! Broth was flavourful, beef was tender. The highlight to me is the wholly new experience! Order the dishes of your choice from the menu on the wall (I had combination pho for 105k dong), then choose the fragrant leaves of your choice (I had lots of basil)... Just take with your hands, tear out the leaves and pop in your pho (don't worry about price). Suqeeze the lime if you like (I squeezed a few drops into my spoonful of noodles and soup right before I put it in my mouth 😄). Add the raw bean sprouts if you like. Take the fried dough fritters (they will somehow calculate when you ask for the bill), take a bite and dunk the open end in the soup, enjoy the next soup-soaked bite, repeat 😆. Also try the brown sauce in the squeeze bottle.

author: Matthew Perry
review_text:
This is the first meal we ate after landing to Vietnam! Everything from Pho to the Ca Phe Sua Da are amazing!  The Pho has a very light and delicate flavorful broth, with a brisket that is so tender.

Banh Bao also brings a tender juicy flavorful filling, the sweet and savory meat really makes the Banh Bao stand out among the other steamed bun I ate before.

The Spring Rolls are also amazing and better if dipped on a sauce. And their Iced Coffee is just what I expected, strong and sweet!

The ambiance is okay, but it is spacious and the staff are kind! The menu that are plastered on the wall was so helpful so that we dont need to ask for the menu everytime!

author: DoublePun
review_text:
A local friend recommended this place, so I gave it a try, and regretted it. I ordered the combination beef pho, fried spring rolls, fresh rolls, and lean pork paste.

The pho itself was mediocre despite the generous portion. The beef was very tough and hard to chew, and the broth was bland and oily. Even my friend admitted it used to be much better.

The fried spring rolls were great, but the fresh rolls were terrible—basically just rice paper filled with vegetables, lacking flavor.

The biggest issue, however, was hygiene. The side vegetables were served on one large shared plate that stayed on the table for different customers before and after us.I literally saw someone grab veggies with their bare hands, then put them back. No replacement. Absolutely disgusting.

Overall, the food was underwhelming, and the low hygiene standards completely ruined the experience for me.

author: Ottotinne
review_text: Delicious! We went here with a group of 10 for some Phở breakfast, we were not disappointed. A good menu and very palatable food & Vietnamese coffee. Seats can fill up pretty quickly, so please be mindful of the time.

author: Christine KIM
review_text:
[Ambiance]
The restaurant is a bit away from the main tourist area, but still quite popular with visitors. Compared to the famous pho spots right in the city center, this place feels much more local and authentic. The space is large and clean. The first floor doesn’t have air conditioning, so it can get a bit warm, while the second floor has AC but it’s quite weak.

[Service]
The staff don’t speak much English, but they understand orders well and the food came out quickly and accurately. They’re not overly friendly like in some touristy restaurants, but they seem hardworking and sincere — focused on getting things done properly.

[Food]
▪︎Fresh Cold Roll – Fresh and clean flavors, with a perfect balance of herbs.
▪︎Spring Roll – The coating was a bit thick for my taste.
▪︎Well Done Brisket – The beef slices were thick and generous, but a bit tough, which made it hard for kids to eat. I wonder if the Raw Beef option would have been more tender.

author: SD
review_text: Pho for breakfast was something I didn’t know I needed. I had the beef brisket pho and the broth was light but had an unbelievable depth of flavour. There were plenty of limes, herbs and sauces available on the table so you could season it to taste. Don’t let the portion deceive you, it’s surprisingly filling with the meat slices and the noodles. I did find the meat slices a little tasteless on their own but not enough to put a damper on the meal.

author: Christian Breitkreutz
review_text: Classic pho place in the heart of the city. This place is quite big: two seating levels. It’s popular by locals as well as tourists. Prices are slightly higher than in other places. But it‘s worth it. I had pho bo tai. The broth was very fragrant and the meat super tender. I also ordered a lot of the Chinese dough. Forgot the name. But I love it!

author: Adriana purwani Sukmawati Azhari
review_text:
Went here in my 2nd day.
I am satisfied with everything.

The food 👍👍👍
Ambience 👍👍👍

Make sure if u travel alone just take the small portion. Cz i didn’t finish my whole bowl, that was really big portion huhu. But the is nice 🫶🏼😻

author: Linh Nguyen
review_text:
Absolutely incredible pho — easily the best I’ve had anywhere. The broth is rich, aromatic, and perfectly balanced — not overly sweet like many places in Australia tend to make it. You can really taste the depth of flavour and the care that’s gone into preparing it.

Everything from the fresh herbs to the tender noodles and meat was spot-on. If you’re a pho lover, this place is a must-try. I’ll definitely be coming back!

author: Ray Sim
review_text:
My food rating guide:
2.5/5 ‐-------> Average taste
5/5 ‐--------> Scrumptious! (My comfort food! 🤩)

Nice bowl of pho. Tender fresh beef and al dente beef ball. Medium bodied savoury soup. Smooth and soft noodle. Clean taste.

The pho was a 4.5/5

author: Li0neL Ng
review_text:
Authentic Vietnamese pho, much much much better than other vietnamese pho in my country... The chilli isn't that spicy. The broth is refreshing & rich of taste

The place surprisingly clean & it's pretty cold in the upstairs coz they have AC & fans

The staff is very friendly even when they have a lot of foreigners visitors

The owner is very kind, he helped me exchanged money from big amount to small amounts

So far this is the BEST pho & Vietnam food I've ate. i ate on 3-4 pho restaurant in totals on this 12 days Vietnam trips

author: Mariah Shane Ng
review_text: It was my first time trying an authentic pho and it was so good! The broth is very tasty and there are a lot of greens that you can add. Just be careful on adding lime can it can really alter the taste. We tried the fresh spring roll. It was so-so. If you are not fond of vegetable, skip it cause the greens are overpowering. The fresh juices are very tasty and refreshing. Lastly, the dough sticks are not free but they'll put it in your table even if you didn't order it. But if you'll not eat it, it will not be charged to you. Will definitely go back before flying back home.

author: tabitha
review_text: i could say this place is tourist friendly since most of the staffs speak little english and they do accept payment by card. food was great, the service was quite good, i just wish they’d explained briefly about how you eat the condiments that were prepared on the table cause i had no clue as it was my first time eating pho

author: Steve Hawkins
review_text:
Great little place that we got recommended by the concierge at the hotel and it didn't disappoint either. Really tasty large portions with a heap of side vegetables to add to your soup. It was 90,000vnd fir the normal size and 105,000vnd for the large. The normal was enough fir us as this was largecto me.
If you're nearby  drop in for a visit for some of the best Pho I've tasted.

author: Thitika K
review_text: I ordered the beef pho, the soup was really good. The beef was tender. On the table there so many sauces, you can add fresh chili and there are many fresh vegetable provided.

author: Ced Aquino
review_text: The pho (d 105k) with a combination of different cuts of beef was delicious. The broth was flavorful pairing well with the fresh greens on the table. The serving was generous and very filling. The apple juice (d 35k) was refreshing though the portion was a bit small. The place is popular with both locals and tourists but the wait time isn't too long.

author: Alex
review_text:
Had this recommended by ChatGPT all the bottom tables were taken, but they have an upstairs section and a section off of that upstairs section which had some seats I got the pho tai chin.
That was delicious. Rich broth and lots of sides to add. I also got the iced tea. That was excellent.

Service was very fast when you’re done they give you a receipt so you can take to pay at the front counter.

Pro tip: bring your own napkins. They charge you 2000 If you use that wet wipe and there’s no napkins on the table.

author: Ragavendra Baburao
review_text:
• One of the most legendary pho spots in Saigon — clean, consistent, and full-bodied broth.
• Tried the brisket bowl and it was the best I’ve ever had
• Locals and expats alike swear by it.
→ Go here if you want a no-fail, OG pho experience.

author: Morgana Lamb
review_text:
10/10 - AMAZING BANH MI, the best we had during our 10 days stay in Vietnam.

Bếp Mẹ In offers a warm and homely taste of authentic Vietnamese cuisine, definitely feel like they came straight from a family kitchen.

Staff were friendly and welcoming, though the wait can be a little longer during peak hours or you can also get a reservation via their website, phone or going there, it is hidden gem at the back alley along with other restaurants. Is not easy to see from the street so go inside of the small street and you will find it.

We had the traditional bah mi and the meatballs one and was FABULOUS. We did not have a reservation so we had to wait around 10 minutes for a table, however was quick and easy to order and to eat. Cannot recommend more. You will love their food. MUST TRY their Banh mi

author: Hungry Happy
review_text: Food is great! They have 3 different concepts in the same lane, bahn mi, noodles and eatery. Queue is long so be sure to make a reservation before going or else be ready to wait. Service is quick and prompt, servers can speak good English and food is great! My must pre-order: bahn mi and beef skewers!

author: Shawn Chua
review_text:
Bếp Mẹ In offers a warm and homely taste of authentic Vietnamese cuisine, with dishes that feel like they came straight from a family kitchen. The flavours are comforting, well-balanced, and not overly commercialized, exactly what you’d hope for from a place that prides itself on tradition.

The menu has a good variety of favourites, from hearty soups to classic rice dishes, and everything is presented beautifully without losing its rustic charm. Portion sizes are generous, and the ingredients taste fresh.

Service is friendly and welcoming, though the wait can be a little longer during peak hours. Prices are reasonable for the quality and atmosphere, making it a solid choice for anyone wanting a reliable Vietnamese meal in a cozy setting. As it is hidden at the back alley along rows of hair salons, you might missed it easily if you did not navigate via Google Maps.

A satisfying and authentic dining experience, definitely worth returning for more.

author: Fatima Jane
review_text:
THIS PLACE IS SERVING DELICIOUS, GOOD QUALITY OF FOOD AT A VERY CHEAP PRICE!!! They truly deserve their Michelin title.

Some would say that the seating arrangement is a little crowded but I really don’t mind. I think it only adds to the authenticity and vibe of the place.

All the vegetables served were fresh and crispy! I loved it. 100/10! Will definitely come back. (Pro tip: Make a reservation!)

author: Yeow Sin Ho
review_text:
This restaurant was listed as a Michelin Bib star so decided to try out during dinner time. I came here with a friend during dinner time at 7pm. There are lot of people but we managed to get a table in about 10 min.

The service here is a bit slow as there is a huge dinner crowd. It took more than 15 min before the staff noticed that we haven order and came to take our order. We ordered a pancake, seafood fried rice and also others. The pancake was really delicious with the rice paper and sauce. The fried rice was well cooked as well.
