author: Wee Loon Chia
review_text:
Followed the Michelin guide to this place. Ordered the recommended shrimp and pork pancake and it did not disappoint. The mixture of everything including the fresh vege wrapped with the rice papers, with the special sauce, it worked perfectly. And that’s the only thing we ordered, other than a can of special Saigon beer, as we were not hungry, and we were glad we did as the pancake serving was a big portion enough for two.

The service was ok. There was one guy at the entrance attending to the new arrivals, and will inform if there is no table available. Table service was great too. The restaurant is located in the alley opposite to the Benh Thanh Market, and has a good vibe!

author: Jhon Melky Chumacera
review_text:
Bếp Mẹ In is one of those rare places that instantly makes you feel like you’ve stepped into everyday life in Ho Chi Minh City rather than a tourist stop. Located conveniently near the market, the restaurant buzzes with energy from morning until evening, filled with locals and visitors alike — a reassuring sign you’re in the right place.

We ordered the bánh xèo, and it absolutely did not disappoint. Perfectly crisp on the outside, fragrant with turmeric, and generously filled, it struck that ideal balance between texture and flavor. Fresh herbs and greens accompanied the dish, making each bite vibrant, satisfying, and unmistakably Vietnamese. The quality of the ingredients really stood out — everything tasted fresh, well-prepared, and made with care.

Despite how busy the restaurant gets, the service remains impressively fast and efficient. Orders come out quickly, staff stay attentive, and the flow of the place never feels chaotic. It’s the kind of organized bustle you only get when a restaurant truly knows what it’s doing.

What makes Bếp Mẹ In special is how authentic the experience feels. Sitting there, surrounded by chatter, sizzling pans, and the rhythm of daily life, you genuinely feel like one of the locals. Great food, great energy, and consistently top-notch quality — a must-visit near the market.

author: Yap Han Lin
review_text:
We had a wonderful dining experience at this Vietnamese restaurant. The food was absolutely delicious. Each dish was well-prepared, flavorful, and truly showcased authentic Vietnamese cuisine.

A special mention goes to the staff, especially Sam, who was attentive and friendly throughout our visit. Sam patiently shared insights about Vietnamese cuisine and helped us understand the dishes better, which made the experience even more enjoyable.

Highly recommended for anyone looking for great food and genuine hospitality.

author: Raymond Lai
review_text:
Pricey, but worth a visit for the food and air conditioning.

This is a good restaurant to experience street foods you find in Vietnam but in a comfortable restaurant setting. Staff knows English well enough to take your order.

Banh xeo is decent, grilled meats are good, and the tumeric fish was moist.

Air conditioning of both the first and second floors.

If you're comfortable with adventuring the truly local street joints, you can skip this restaurant.

author: Cristian Patru
review_text: Great food and drinks, stopped by spontaneously after visiting the Independence Palace, as it's in walking distance and was totally worth it. Big portions, we had some fried pork as a starter and as main a Cha Ca La Vong (fried snakehead fish fillets) and a Banh Mi. I have to admit, it was too much, we couldn't finish. Food tastes amazing and the Pineapple juice was great. Highly recommend this place!

author: Vicky Kuo
review_text: I ate here twice and loved both times! Really delicious food, quick service and decently friendly staff. Pricier than local street food, obviously, but still cheap and worth it in my opinion. Get the beef skewers - best meal I’ve had in HCMC.

author: Dwight Kenneth
review_text:
Let’s start off with the good!

Food was fresh and came out SUPER FAST! Portion sizes were great too! We were greeted and seated promptly as we already had reservations. Another great thing is the variety that they offer , they have a plethora of authentic Vietnamese dishes. Lots of the dishes tasted amazing !

The not so good, some of the dishes weren’t the tastiest. The Bahn Xeo in my personal opinion is pretty over hyped here. We also tried the summer rolls, and they weren’t that good either (the sauce they came with was amazing though) The prices were a LOT higher than that of what you would normally paid.

Overall, it’s a pretty decent experience. But for the fact that they offer so much variety maybe it compromises on the quality of certain dishes. I also think that it has a lot of height, even though there’s locals and tourist here. The price of value ratio for me just wasn’t there.

author: Minh Nguyễn Hoàng
review_text:
The restaurant has a clean and comfortable atmosphere. The staff are friendly, polite, and provide quick service, especially the staff member Tan Si
The food is served promptly and looks very appealing. The taste is well-balanced and delicious, matching my expectations.
Prices are reasonable for the quality. A great place to enjoy a meal with friends or family.
I will definitely come back again.

author: Joe and Mindy
review_text:
From Bánh Mì to Bliss: Bếp Mẹ Ỉn, the Sister Restaurant You Can't Miss

If you loved Bánh Mì Mẹ Ỉn (and you should!), then Bếp Mẹ Ỉn, its sister restaurant just steps away, is an absolute must-try. Nestled in an alley (picture we attached )near Ben Thanh Market, this hidden gem is well worth seeking out.
I had the Nem Nuong Me In, minced pork wrapped in rice paper with fresh veggies and Thai basil, and it was an explosion of flavor! It quickly became one of my favorite dishes in Saigon, a perfect harmony of amazing tastes. Today was the day I fell head over heels for Vietnamese cuisine.
The restaurant's location adds to its charm, creating an intimate and authentic atmosphere. The staff is friendly and attentive, making the dining experience even more enjoyable.
Overall, Bếp Mẹ Ỉn is a culinary adventure that will leave you craving more. Don't miss out on this hidden gem when you're in Saigon!

author: Catalina Altomonte
review_text: Such a delicious Vietnamese pancake! Also had the yummiest goi cuon here. Broken rice was also a winner and loved how tasty the pork was. Everything felt really light and fresh, and especially loved all the dipping sauce. Came a peak lunch hour and the waiting time moved much faster than expected.

author: chaoyue
review_text:
Reserved a spot the day before and was seated upstairs (would recommend a reservation). First thing I noticed was that the table was a bit wobbly and that there doesn't seem like there was a place to put down our bags, though that is a minor detail.

Many thanks to the waitress Vy who attended to our table promptly as well as the server who taught us how to properly eat the bahn xeo.

Now on to the food, we ordered the Banh xeo, broken rice with grilled pork, and the fried pork in bamboo  with white sesame. I'd recommend all of them but the Banh xeo is definitely a must try. Ask your waiter/server for the proper steps to eat the dish. The sauce also pairs well with it.
As for the broken rice, we had to ask a waiter for a spoon which I think could be improved. (not sure if we were supposed to eat in some other way?)
The sweet sauce (to be poured over the rice) also does make the food more appetising.
Lastly, the fried pork was nice and the sauce made it even more delicious, but I think the sauce provided was too little.

Still, overall experience was great. Food was served so fast I was not prepared.

author: SM
review_text: I didn’t see what’s the hype on this place. The food tasted average to me. You can get it anywhere else that serve the similar food. If there’s no wait in line, you can try it. But if you need to wait for hour, save your time and eat elsewhere. Service is slow. Payment needs to pay twice (drinks and food, separately and different location). It’s a hassle with the right space.

author: Angelica Beth Sia
review_text: Food serving is huge, and food is just divine! Best bun cha ever. The service is also excellent. From how they received us (despite no reservations) and server us with all smiles, we enjoyed the experience all the way. Special mention to the best crew teka, sam, and alexander! Thank you so much

author: Hernalisa Phang
review_text: Really enjoy the food with my family, we order 9 dishes and we like 8 of those. The best is pork fried. The drink, white coffee is also nice. The service is fast and friendly. Recommended to come and try everything that must try. You must reserve before come because it is always full.

author: Martine MT
review_text:
Wonderful place – we’ll for sure be coming back!

Even though we didn’t book a table in advance, we were seated immediately. The staff were warm, attentive, and very accommodating when it came to food allergies, which we truly appreciated.

We were told the food would take around 15 minutes, but it arrived much quicker – a pleasant surprise! And it was fantastic – full of flavor and beautifully presented. Sharing several small dishes is a great way to enjoy the variety on the menu.

We wholeheartedly recommend this spot. Already looking forward to our next visit!

author: Kenzie Winther
review_text: All the reviews are spot on. So much meat on one sandwich. They are popular so they have it down to a science. You order at one window. Wait in line to pick up at another. There is an eating area next door. You are paying more money but the sandwich is FULL of meat. They give you the toppings in a bag so you get to make it yourself. It was a delicious sandwich and I wouldn’t hesitate to get it again.

author: Liz
review_text: Bánh Mì Huỳnh Hoa is hands down one of the best bánh mì spots in Saigon. From the moment you take your first bite, you can taste the quality in every layer. The baguette is perfectly crispy on the outside and soft inside, packed generously with a rich variety of cold cuts, pate, fresh herbs, and house-made sauces. Each component is well-balanced, flavorful, and incredibly satisfying. Despite being famous and often busy, the service is quick and efficient. One bánh mì is filling enough for a full meal. If you’re looking for an unforgettable, authentic Vietnamese bánh mì experience, Huỳnh Hoa is an absolute must-try.

author: Daniel Ravelo Mejia
review_text: You have to come and try it! Without a doubt, the best Vietnamese bánh mì in Ho Chi Minh City! The menu is super simple: just one type of bánh mì, no customization options, but the portion is huge, ideal for sharing between two. The dough is perfectly crispy, covered with a rich pork liver pâté, layered with ham, pork aspic, and fresh vegetables 🥬 (served separately to add). Super tasty and satisfying! I highly recommend it. Just one costs 73,000 VND, approximately $2.77. It's worth it. It's close to the center, very easy to get to. One is enough, but with two breads, it's a delight.

author: JC M
review_text:
Mixed feelings on this one. I was expecting it to easily be a top ten best Banh Mi I’ve ever had (having never been to Vietnam prior to this trip).

It was a good sandwich, but I’ve had much better Banh Mi’s in the US - not even in cities known for Vietnamese food. This is a high volume, large portion thing. If that is what you are going for you will be very happy.

Pros:
- Pate was maybe the best I’ve had on a Banh Mi
- Meats were plentiful, thick cut and tasty
- Amazing value and speed
- Thoughtful to go packing with vegetables separated to ensure the baguette didn’t get soggy

Cons:
- not balanced at all as most Vietnamese food is
- bread had beyond the crunch you want, maybe I just got a bad baguette but it was crunchy to the point it could shred the top of your mouth
- vegetables did not add the texture and balance I desire in a Banh Mi
- peppers were terribly cut with a huge variety in thickness, resulting in some bites with a lot of heat and some bites with none

author: Pedram Nick Aryan
review_text:
Viral for a reason, but maybe not the right one … case of volume over quality.

If you’re coming here because of TikTok, just know what you’re getting into: a massive meat mountain. It’s takeaway only and no seating.

The Pro: The portion size is insane. They give you the veggies in a separate bag, which is a smart move to keep the bread from getting soggy during transport. The kitchen looks clean and staff were polite, friendly and quick.

The Con: It’s almost too much meat. The flavor profile is heavy and lacks that light, herbal balance of a traditional banh mi. The bread was also a bit of a letdown, lacking that signature airy crunch.

Verdict: There’s no denying the "wow" factor when they hand you this heavy bag. However, after the first few bites, the novelty wears off. It’s a fun "bucket list" item for the sheer scale of it, but as far as flavor goes? It's mediocre. Unfortunately, the sandwich itself misses the mark on the fundamentals and the delicate balance Saigon’s street food is known for. It’s a bit of a "stunt food" experience.

author: Christopher Wu
review_text:
From Melbourne, which already has a pretty strong banh mi game, I had to give this spot a try after seeing it hyped all over social media. Tried the mixed ham banh mi — I’ve never seen one packed with this much meat before, it was absolutely loaded.

Flavour-wise though, it didn’t quite hit for me. It was a bit too full-on and the balance just wasn’t there. They give you salad on the side to add into the banh mi, which helps freshen it up, but the bread didn’t have that signature crisp I look for. Probably because they’re pumping them out so fast, so the consistency can vary — still decent overall though.

Queued up for about 10 minutes — they’re efficient and move quick. The banh mi itself is massive, easily shareable between two people. Towards the end, the texture got a bit weird on mine, might’ve just been my roll, but I wasn’t a fan. Definitely could’ve used more chilli or a spice kick.

For around $5, you can’t really complain, but coming from Melbourne’s already strong banh mi scene, I was expecting a bit more given the hype.

author: Romano Pravdič
review_text:
1. It’s GIANT. Definitely for 2 people
2. It’s filled with a TON of ham and meat

Beware! It’s good, but just too much filling for my taste, had to throw the other half away as I could not eat it 😬 Also not enough vegetables to balance the flavors. Service is fast.

But it you want to get as full as possible, 73k VND is an unbeatable price.

There is no “dine-in”, just takeout.

author: Denis X.
review_text: Probably one of the better bahn mis i have had in ho chi minh!! The queue was insane but it clears quite quickly so don’t worry about that. There is a dedicated sitting section but it was so oacked that we decided to takeaway and have it at one of the cafes opposite the street alongside some vietnamese coffee. Highly recommended!!

author: Nicole Quek
review_text:
Gigantic portion - can be shared between two or even three pax.

Based on what I see, at least four different types of ham was used. The pate is pretty good, though the floss was not evenly spread.

Fresh vegetables served in separate sealed plastic bags.

The service was fast and there’s a small unit between their two kitchens with seats for customers.

author: Day dreamer
review_text: Absolutely the best Vietnamese bánh mì in Ho Chi Minh! The menu is super simple—just one type of bánh mì, no customizations, but the portion is huge, easily enough for two to share. The crust is perfectly crispy, slathered with rich pork liver pâté, layered with ham, pork jelly, and fresh veggies 🥬 (served separately to add yourself). So flavorful and satisfying! Highly recommend!

author: Kenny Tang
review_text:
Famous bánh mì spot in HCM — and the sandwiches are huge! The shop runs almost like a mini factory, with staff constantly assembling bánh mì. A loaded pork-and-ham one costs 75,000 VND. The pickles and garnishes are given separately for you to add yourself. From what I could tell, it’s takeaway only.

The baguette was nicely crunchy, though the size made it a bit hard to eat — it would probably be even better if it were about a third smaller. The meats blended well and the pâté was tasty. I added all the garnishes, including the chillies, and it came together nicely.

It’s clearly a well-known spot in HCM, with queues outside and a steady stream of Grab drivers picking up orders.

Worth trying if you’re in the area, but I’m not sure I’d make a special trip for it. There are so many bánh mì options in the city, and plenty of them are also very good.

author: Mink Marks
review_text:
I got lucky and got mine in 3 minutes waiting in line.  Im a big eater , 210 pound guy :), and i was completely stuffed after 1. Might even be a bit of a meat overdose.. but it was good. Pricer than on the street but as a tourist its still nothing for such a filling.

Takeaway only, veggies etc on the side. Loads of plastics come with that ofcourse…

author: Michelle Pham
review_text: The best banh mi place I had while exploring Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City! Its pricier than most banh mi in the city but its worth is. The bread amazing,meat cuts thick, pate delicious. The banh mi is huge. I ate half for lunch and ate the other half for dinner.

author: vu nguyen
review_text: Tourist spot that is always packed. Banh mi is a little on the pricier side at around 75k but these monstrosity of a Sammie is basically 3 meals. All though the lines are long, the service is quick as they only make 1 style of sandwich. Apparently this is one of the 2 most popular spots in Saigon and they were both ex lovers but who knows. They make a good Sammie though.

author: Khanh Vu Huu
review_text:
I visited Banh Mi Huynh Hoa for the first time after seeing all the hype on Social Media. The sandwich costs 73,000 VND and is definitely huge and generously filled. For my taste, though, it was too generously filled, there was so much pâté and mayonnaise that it squeezed out of the bread with every bite.

The shop had a good idea by packing the herbs and vegetables separately to keep the bread from getting soggy during transport, but unfortunately this creates an extreme amount of plastic waste since every single ingredient comes in its own little bag. A more sustainable alternative would really make sense here.

Flavor-wise, the banh mi was okay, but definitely not worth the hype. I’ve had much better banh mi‘s in Saigon since then.

author: Shmiley C
review_text:
I would say this is a must try in HCMC for a massive banh mi.

The long line should be an indicator that this place knows what's up. The price of the banh mi is higher than the price at street cart vendors because the quantity is bigger here. Banh mi dac biet is 73,000 VND.

Wait in line to order first. *Cash only. Then pick up order inside. You can take the food away or there is indoor seating in the room to the right side. It's messy! They separate the veggies.

CASH ONLY
No wifi

author: Mrgrc
review_text:
I travelled through Vietnam for three weeks. And this was the worst Bahn Mi I've eaten! Since it was described as 'the best', I gave it a chance. I have eaten better and cheaper than here while travelling.

+ Everything is thrown on a pile? Vegetables are wrapped in plastic... Not a good experience for me.

author: Manuel Dresselmann
review_text:
If you are looking for a great banh mi experience look no further. The incredibly long queue to the Shop speaks for itself.

The Portion of banh mi that you get is so full of ingredients such as: ruoc, lots of butter, rich paté and its signature sausage that half a sandwhich is enough for most.

If that as it is wouldnt be enough you also get different sides to create your perfect banh mi. 1 Pack of pickles, 1 Pack of cucumber and 1 Pack with a mix of spring Onion, coriander and Chili.

This shop truely understands how to serve the national dish.

author: Edmond Khor
review_text:
Best banh mi i ever had. There are 3 shops belong to them beside each other(2 kitchen and 1 dining area).

You can also bring the banh mi across the road to have it in the other cafe.

author: Ha Tran
review_text:
Got the order as take-away and veggies packages always included, fresh pickles, onions, pate and the banhmi itself is always top-notch. The waiting line was long but efficient-organized line made it fast!!

As a local and been having Huynh Hoa since the banhmi was around 45.000 VND until now, I gotta say the price goes with the quality. The portion is huge, 2-3persons/portion so recommend to share it or big eater!!

author: Ni
review_text:
This rooftop restaurant is worth checking out if you can find it's discreet entrance. Once we found it, we walked up several flights of stairs. There was friendly service and some delicious food, despite a mix up on one of the orders. There is not much of a view though.
There is no gluten free menu available.

author: Christopher Yandell
review_text: The food here is really delicious, I highly recommend the soba noodles and beef skewers. The sauces that all of the dishes are served with are definitely a highlight. It’s kind of hard to find as it’s on the top floor of a relatively inconspicuous building but if you find it, it is definitely worth it.

author: MR DL
review_text: Very hidden! After walking up a number of stairs, you're rewarded by a fabulous private terrace with wonderful locally made food, set against a fantastic skyline. The service is excellent and the food is superb. A great place to dine. Not noisy, calm and respectful. Give it a go... and keep it secret!

author: Elijah Chell
review_text: We were thoroughly impressed with the food; it was much better than we anticipated. The staff deserves major praise. They were incredibly helpful in coordinating a small, instant surprise for our friend and even assisted us with a last-minute cake order. Thank you for the wonderful service!

author: Penny Gaffney
review_text:
We were looking for place for a light meal before going to water puppet show and had this restaurant on the way from our hotel on the list.
The restaurant located on the 6th floor of sort of a residential looking apartment building.
There is a restaurant name sign in front of the building. But first you have to walk into sort of an apartment courtyard with many motorcycles packed walkway.
The view on the top was very nice. It's mostly open outdoor restaurant with a moveable roof for sun and rain. Lovely bit of garden in the middle of the place.
We had 3 dishes to share between the 3 of us, squid herbs salad, grilled fish with garden salad, and steam lemongrass clams. We also had 2 desserts to finish off the meal, some coconut mix beans with green chewie and a longan mix dried fruits sweet. The food was okay and the place is very relaxing. However there were not really anything I can called service, as it was hard to even find the staff to order food with.

author: Sunnyside Up
review_text: Good atmosphere but mainly the tourists. Food generally pretty good with big variety but size can be quite large to try more than a few dishes. Though on my visit, they have an extra dish on my bill. When notes a correct bill was given, a little too quickly. So ensure you check thoroughly.

author: Kamal J
review_text: Had fun time finding this place and climbing more than a few flights of stairs. We ordered the chicken main dish and I was unable to eat it due to the toughness of the meat. My friends also were very disappointed in their meals. Cocktails were good. My one and only meal that I wasn’t able to eat on my whole south east Asia tour! Disappointed

author: Joana
review_text:
An amazing dining area with a lovely bar and a fantastic vibe.
Excellent food and a lovely selection of home made Vietnamese cuisines.
The service is superb and the staff are very friendly.

author: James Wilson
review_text: Secret Garden is a charming little oasis in the middle of District 1. The greenery and cozy setup make it perfect for relaxing with a coffee or catching up with friends. The drinks are well-made and the staff is friendly. A lovely spot to unwind in the city.

author: katie Weston
review_text: Lovely rooftop atmosphere. Several vegetarian options (made fresh rice paper rolls upon request). Would come again. Able to get a walk in about 5:30pm

author: kkkami
review_text: This place is really secret! All of the staff is really friendly and helpful. The restaurant is located on the top of the building, so you have to go up stairs but it’s worth! All of dishes are delicious!

author: A T
review_text: A place where you can get all the kind of Vietnam food at higher prices. It’s still affordable and location is quite central. Rooftop vibes and would be more suitable at night. The spring rolls are delicious. But the char siew (pork) is normal.

author: Peter Vogelsanger
review_text: Brilliant food. Be aware that you have to walk up 8 sets of stairs, no elevator. But you'll be ready for a cold drink and it's definitely worth it 😉👍

author: Janne Smeets
review_text:
Super nice place in district 1 Saigon .
It wasn’t super easy to find but we loved the food. Atmosphere was amazing with views over the city.
Vegetarian friendly!

author: Danielle Cusnir
review_text:
This is an amazing hidden gem! Keep going up the stairs and yoh will find this cute secret garden.

Food wise I order a salad which I was never told it was super spicy! When I complained the waiter told me he had never eaten the salad so he did not know it was spicy, but he would not be able to refund or change. I mean, waiters must know the menu even ifthey haven’t tried all food. As I could not eat it I order a sticky rice toasg with pork on top. The portions are really small and quite pricy for Ho Chi Minh city! There are more options with bigger better food and prices. The place is amazing for a drink, but service and food wise is not worth it.

author: J L
review_text: Okay, I didn't want to write but I was asked. We were not made aware of the holiday surcharge. The rice was a bit tasteless and we couldn't chew the pork. Atmosphere and views were good, however not worth 4 flights of stairs and this price.

author: Florian Kowarsch
review_text:
Hidden gem with authentic Vietnamese food & cozy scenery. Helpful service.
Just be prepared to receive all dishes at once & there is a lot to eat & choose from.

author: Summer C
review_text: while i do agree it’s a tourist trap, the spring rolls platter was fabulous. centrally located, and yes there’s that stair climb. we had lunch so we reckon it’s nicer at night but the spring rolls was such a great welcome to saigon

author: Duj Štokić
review_text: Too expensive for the quality and the taste, for the starter we took spring rolls and they were OK, but for the main course we took their sausages and a vietnamese pancake with beef. Sausages were sweet ( not our thing) so we cant judge but the pancake was filled with like a kilo of cabbage and 3 small pieces of beef. Overall too expensive and we went home hungry.

author: Juaquin Gerton-Henderson
review_text: Went here two nights ago and have to say it’s one of the best places we’ve found. All the flights of stairs were most definitely worth it. We arrived and got seated in a waiting area as we didn’t have a reservation. It was no more than 2 minutes that we had to wait to be seated at a table. Ordered and the food was fantastic. Me and my friend who went were trying to eat on a budget and we found the cheaper items to be on the leg pages. Less fancy but still very good. Great portion great taste, great flavours. The atmosphere was the best part in my opinion, perched on a roof top overlooking the tops of some of the Saigon buildings. We went on a Friday night and it was bustling…but not overpoweringly loud. Overall great experience, would highly recommend if your around the area.

author: Tran Vinh Phuc
review_text:
Nhà Hàng Ngon

Great place to experience a wide variety of traditional Vietnamese dishes in one location. The menu is extensive, covering specialties from different regions, and everything we tried was well-prepared and flavorful.

The grilled fish was perfectly cooked with a nice balance of spices, the fried rice was fragrant and not greasy, and the clam soup was light, aromatic, and comforting. Desserts were also a highlight—classic Vietnamese sweets done right, not overly sweet.

The atmosphere is lively and authentic, making it ideal for both tourists and locals who want to explore Vietnamese cuisine. Service was efficient despite the restaurant being quite busy.

Prices are reasonable for the quality and variety offered. Highly recommended if you want a reliable introduction to Vietnamese food in a comfortable setting.

author: Pattararatda
review_text:
A popular - touristy - restaurant right in the heart of District 1, with a menu that spans local, fusion, and broader Asian cuisine.

The food isn't up to my personal liking but it does a great job of catering to diverse groups.  I, however, love their innovative and excellent drink menus (btw the vietnamese coffee is crazily strong!).

Service is impeccable.  Be prepared for a crowd, this place is huge but super popular.

author: vu nguyen
review_text: Huge elegant restaurant that feels like a chateau with a massive outdoor seating arraignment.  Large menu selection that has a little bit of everything from a vietnamese cuisine perspective. My mom and aunt ordered the hot pot with fish and baked fish, while I ordered the pork in the clay pot. Would definitely go again.

author: Abraham Lee
review_text: Ngon offers a semi-outdoor dining experience that was cool and relaxing in the evening, though it might feel a bit warm on a hotter day. The setting is immaculate .. beautifully decorated and almost like stepping into someone’s grand home. The food was decent, and while the staff had limited English proficiency, they were attentive and helpful. Overall, it was a pleasant and impressive place to dine.

author: Randall Huskinson
review_text: Really special environment. Excellent food quality. I asked out tour company to arrange upscale lunch someplace our group could try a variety of Vietnamese dishes beyond pho. This place knocked of out of the park. The food was fresh and delicious and a real balance of dishes including meat, fish, and veggies. The space itself is wildly creative and welcoming. Would definitely return!

author: CHENIS SS
review_text:
The restaurant has a lovely atmosphere with beautiful decor. Most of the area is semi-outdoor, which can get a bit warm depending on the season, but it still feels cozy and relaxing. The place is quite spacious and can host many guests. There’s also a second floor that’s quieter and more peaceful — perfect if you want a calm dining experience.

The staff are kind and helpful, though their English communication is a bit limited.

The food tastes good overall 🍽️, but a few dishes seemed not freshly prepared (a little cold and not very warm). Still, everything was flavorful and enjoyable.

author: CJ Lawrence - CliveyBwoy
review_text:
Ngon is very cool, in the heart of the city it’s a pretty busy place so maybe a reservation might be best.

We arrived just looking for a table for 3 and waited a short while (no more than 5 minutes) before being guided to our table.

It’s a big restaurant, stunning decor, family friendly with a very relaxed atmosphere.

The menu is extensive, there is plenty to choose from, it’s not all traditional dishes, there a western mix too.

I can’t remember the dish I ordered but it was a seafood salad, being it was still early lunch time.

The prices seemed fair, I guess, it took a little while to arrive (but it was busy) but I have to say I had more salad than seafood and was slightly disgruntled that the balance wasn’t quite there. That’s when I started to question the price. Did I just pay 100k for a lot of cucumber? 🤣

Anyway, delicious as it was I was totally blown away by the decor.

The walls are a deep, sensual red, making it ideal for a hot date, the lighting and garden, pond area are just visually breathtaking and really set the tone.

I saw many families, a few couples and just groups of friends hanging out so this restaurant really caters for everyone.

The staff were attentive and polite and brought out the baby seat for the little one, so we were made to feel comfortable and were never made to feel ignored or forced to holler for anything we needed.

A good experience overall, and a happy tummy if not a very appreciative wallet.

But you can’t have it all eh!

author: Keerati Lakakum
review_text: The food here is flavorful and well-prepared, with a wide variety of dishes to choose from. Prices are reasonable and in line with the standard. The staff provide great service, making the overall dining experience very enjoyable. This is definitely a must-visit spot for anyone coming to Ho Chi Minh City.

author: EC Chan
review_text: Authentic Vietnamese food at very reasonable price for such cosy and nice ambience. They served Thai and Chinese cuisine too but I was focusing just their Vietnamese dishes and never disappoint with it. Service was not too bad but can be improved because there were quite busy during lunch time. Food quality is top notch and the price is reasonable. Will definitely come back again

author: Tee Wang
review_text: Every time I come back to visit Vietnam, this would be the first restaurant that I stop by before venturing out to try all the street foods. Of course the prices in here are a bit more than other restaurants but you’re paying for the view, the services, and the beautiful interior. It’s quite cozy. After a long flight, I just want to relax first before experiencing eating in the hot weather of Vietnam. 😆 It’s an overall a great experience. I love their variety of drinks.

author: Andrew Goh
review_text:
This restaurant offers traditional Vietnamese cuisine and features charming decor inspired by traditional Vietnamese architecture. The seating is small and closely packed, and there is no air conditioning—only fans—so visiting during summer in Ho Chi Minh City might be challenging.

The fried spring rolls, supposedly a signature Vietnamese dish, were disappointing due to their lack of crispiness; the skin didn’t crack as expected and stuck unpleasantly when eaten. The fresh spring rolls were also underwhelming, with tough wraps that were difficult to bite through, likely due to being pre-prepared and dried out.

The steamed sea snails were bland, and the mango salad was just average. The grilled chicken lacked proper marination, though the boiled chicken stood out with its flavorful and tasty meat. The so-called “king” dish, tapioca with luncheon meat, was bland and not something I would recommend. The spicy fried squid was a letdown, as the overcooked squid became chewy.

On a positive note, the baked crab was an impressive dish, although the crab meat could have been more flavorful. Overall, the dining experience was mixed, with a few highlights but many areas for improvement.

author: Cee ee
review_text:
We ordered appetizers as soon as we arrived, and they were served quickly. However, the experience went downhill with the main course. Only my companion’s dish was served, and I had to wait almost an hour for mine. When we followed up, we were repeatedly told it would be “5 more minutes,” but the wait kept getting longer. When my food finally arrived, it was no longer hot. The server also seemed upset when I said I no longer wanted to eat it, even though we still paid the bill. Overall, this was a disappointing experience. Not recommended.

Consider hiring staff who can speak and understand English clearly. Good communication is essential for providing proper service, and it should not be this difficult.

author: Genesis Macale
review_text:
Best bun cha I've eaten in Vietnam, having visited this country thrice. I wanted to come back just to eat this again there! The service was very fast too.

The place generally felt like a palace. So large and so many people.

author: Aaron Tay
review_text: Food was very tasty and authentic. The ambience is very nice and the staff are very attentive. Great place to bring colleagues and international visitors. While this is a little pricey compared to other local establishments, it is still reasonable for the portions (Asian size please).

author: Vei Vei
review_text:
This restaurant is very popular with both tourists and locals. It offers a spacious setting with both indoor and outdoor seating, kept cool mainly by fans.

The staff is numerous and fairly quick, though not particularly friendly. The menu is diverse, and while the prices are high, they are reasonable given the restaurant’s location and reputation.
However, if you're looking for typical local dishes at budget-friendly prices, you might want to think twice before dining here.

author: Aaron Pham
review_text:
Ngon Restaurant in Ho Chi Minh City has an impressively large menu with plenty of options to choose from. The food quality is great overall, and I especially enjoyed the hacao dumplings—they’re generously sized and flavorful. The snail dishes are also worth trying if you’re looking for something unique.

That said, I felt the prices were a bit on the higher side compared to the portions and overall value, but the taste and presentation did make up for it. The staff are quick and attentive, which makes the dining experience smooth, and it’s very convenient that they accept card payments here.

Overall, I walked away pretty happy with the experience—a good mix of variety, quality, and efficient service, even if the prices felt slightly elevated.

author: Bożena Wróblewska
review_text: Wonderful Asian cuisine, including excellent Vietnamese dishes, served in beautifully designed interiors. The décor is rich in flowers and greenery – artificial, yet tastefully arranged. Elegant, cozy, and full of details that create an atmosphere of luxury and comfort. A perfect spot for a special dinner

author: Rosie C
review_text: Decent place for big groups and all rounded Vietnamese cuisine. Music was too loud for my liking, could barely hear my lunch guests over it. And was difficult to get hold of a waitress as they seemed understaffed. Food was tasty though!

author: Charles Bronson (CNorris)
review_text: It was all very good but pricey compared to similar nearby. However the place is an open air with misters sort of place so not too hot but still humid. Ate with a 8+ crod and was good. But didn't stand out above. Maybe I should have tried the octopus.

author: Art
review_text:
I loved the food but dishes came out at different times and the service had some small issues. Not much AC, kinda hit.

Edit: I went back a second time simply because it was convenient and was sorely disappointed, which had caused me to lower my review to a 3 star. When we arrived we didn’t seem to have an assigned waitress, no one came to take our order or greet us for a while until I was more aggressively looking at waitstaff near me so someone would come. Two waitresses seemed confused in who was supposed to take our orders until one finally came over. The waitress was courteous, but we never saw her again. No one came to check on our meals at all. When the meal finally came it was not as good as the meal I first ordered the other day. I was a little disappointed because the image was different than the reality. I was expecting peas, baby corns, and broccoli with my dish from the image but instead got heaps of mushrooms, celery, and onions with some broccoli and other veggies. Though strangely only two tiny pieces of red pepper?  It didn’t explicitly say which vegetables we would get, but I was less enthused. Overall I didn’t feel like I received good service, perhaps because I’m a foreigner, and since I’ve gone two times and received bad service both times, I feel like these are not isolated incidents. Also, the food came out at different times again. Though the restaurant is absolutely gorgeous and the staff were pleasant, and the food wasn’t terrible.

author: Jessie Lan Pham
review_text: I’ve ordered from Cơm Tấm Ba Ghiền twice and tried both the grilled pork chop and the grilled chicken. The toppings are genuinely good, and as someone who really loves com tam and has tried many places, I can see why Ba Ghiền is so well known. That said, I think the experience is best when you customize it a bit to suit your own taste. Personally, I find the grilled chicken juicier and less dry than the pork chop. The rice is on the drier side and clearly meant to be eaten with soup. Since I usually skip the soup, I add a little water and microwave the rice when eating at home, to make it softer. One small tip is to order outside peak hours, either before or after lunch or dinner, as the food tends to be prepared more carefully. For example, when I ordered around 9 am and asked for extra chili, they were very generous.

author: Tim Chu
review_text: I am surprised with the four stars rating of this location. This definitely is one of the best place to enjoy a simple rice dish with nicely cooked, charred, and juicy meat to go with it. The location is relatively far away from all the tourist places, but that's exactly why we travel and explore the unknowns. Very easy menu here and the prices are extremely reasonable.

author: Chong khai tjie
review_text:
Forget about the Michelin Guide. This was one of the juiciest and most flavourful pork chops I've had ANYWHERE. The reviewers leaving anything less than 5 stars don't know what they are talking about.

I got the mixed platter and it was incredible. Every single ingredient was done perfectly and was an explosion of flavours in my mouth. I just wished I had more stomach space to eat an extra portion of everything. The pork chop was infused with a delicious smoky aroma, while being sweet and juicy at the same time. The pork skin, pork sausage, pickled vegetables, fried egg, and egg loaf (they call it "roll") were all masterpieces in their own right. Combined together with the soft broken rice into a huge and hearty plate, it was well worth every single cent.

Please find time to visit this place if you're in HCM! It seems to be a family run business and they know what they are doing. They do grabfood as well if you can't find the time to go down in person.

author: yumz
review_text:
cơm tấm ba ghiền is that spot that just gets it right

the plate of dreams //
this ain't your average broken rice situation. for the uninitiated, cơm tấm uses fragrant grains of rice that were once considered fractured or broken, creating a uniquely tender texture that's pure comfort. the sizzling pork chop hits different. crispy edges, juicy inside, and that legendary fish sauce glaze that's straight fire. they absolutely don't skimp on portions either, serving up a pork rib that's noticeably larger than what you'll find at most other spots. heads up though. the marinade leans sweet, which might be a bit much if you prefer savory-forward flavors like i do. crack that runny egg over the rice and prepare for a flavor explosion.

the real deal vibe //
no frills, just pure energy. the place is always buzzing, plates clattering, and the aroma will have your stomach screaming yes. you order at the counter, grab a plastic stool, and dive into pure food joy.

the final call //
if you want to taste a true saigon classic that never misses, this is the move. be prepared to wait during peak hours. it's that popular for a reason. michelin bib gourmand.

don't forget to ❤️.

author: Anshika Prasad
review_text:
The Com Tâm was phenomenal. I’m back to my country and I’m still craving it! Someone said forget Michelin guide, this is the best pork ever, anywhere! And I agree. Amazing flavours, beautifully done meat! The sauce pairs well, we visited and had some. And within 3 hours we ended up ordering again via grab to have it again.
We also had the strawberry smoothie and it was a lot, and very delicious!
I’m tempted to come back to HCMC to have the ribs.

author: Michael Chu
review_text: The Suon Bi Op La was delicious and the place is welcoming.  Nice open concept with plenty of seating.  Food was cooked fresh and you can taste the variety of flavors.  One of the best combo rice plates that I’ve had here in Saigon.

author: Niles Cong
review_text: Best Cơm Tấm in-town. If you are looking for an extremely full and delicious dinner to fill up an empty stomach, this is the place you want to give it a try. The seats are okay, but the main dish was absolutely without a doubt. The toppings are many, and you may have to order additional portion of rice to finish the remaining. The serving was quite fast and waiters were energetic. The only downside is thr price is a bit high for the dish with full topping.

author: Eric K
review_text:
Decent size restaurant.

Food (10/10) - Best pork chop broken rice tasted so far. Large piece of pork provided.

Price (9/10) - Good value for the serving size provided.

Service (9/10) - Staffs were friendly with very limited English.

Ambience (7/10) - It was quite clean and spacious inside. Floor was slippery and not air conditioned.

Will definitely be back again.

author: Andrew J
review_text: Food was mediocre at best. We were served almost immediately after sitting down, which made it clear the meat wasn’t freshly grilled — especially surprising when you can see the chef grilling right behind the seating area. Some people might prefer the quick service, but I personally would have preferred freshly grilled meat. Overall an okay meal, and the prices were good, so no complaints there.

author: Andrew Limo
review_text:
Had a scrumptious super sized breakfast here with a couple of buddies and it did not disappoint. The pork chop was grilled to perfection as was the sausage, the fried egg tasted so nice and the ABC soup that accompanied the dish was another highlight. I also ordered their "kiam chye" soup because I was curious and it was delicious.
Overall, if you are looking for comfort food that uses homemade recipe and cooking style .... this place will blow you away for sure.
Best thing is that it is so CHEAP ....... ENJOY !!!!!!!

author: Joseph
review_text: Our first Michelin spot in Vietnam — and it definitely lived up to the hype! The grilled pork with broken rice was flavorful, juicy, and perfectly cooked. Simple but so satisfying. Fast service, friendly staff, and that authentic local vibe you can’t beat. Totally worth the visit!

author: kazu-kun
review_text:
I visited a long-established Cơm Tấm restaurant in Ho Chi Minh City for the first time. The restaurant is featured in the Michelin guide, so I went there with high expectations. The restaurant had a spacious area with about 40 seats, but it was very crowded even when I visited around 1:30 PM.
You can order in Vietnamese, a little English, and by pointing and using gestures. There are only six basic set menus, so it's easy to order.
The food arrived in two minutes after I ordered. It's very speedy. The taste of the Cơm Tấm was characterized by its sweet sauce. The pork was very large and quite substantial, which might be too much for some women.
The restaurant lacks a sense of cleanliness in appearance. During busy times, it's common to find trash on the floor, and there's a slight smell of food waste. Some customers were smoking while walking. However, this is a common sight in long-established local restaurants, so if you've visited Vietnam several times, it shouldn't be a problem. Japanese people visiting for the first time might experience a bit of culture shock.
If you want to eat a lot of Cơm Tấm cheaply, I think Cơm Tấm enthusiasts will find it worth repeating!

author: Fluke Chan
review_text: Ever since I have been coming to HCM since 2012, I’ll start by saying that I used to argue with people that com tam ba ghien was better than com tam van cu. I am not sure what has happened to the food quality, but just had delivered what looks like boiled pork chops and an over cooked egg. Ba ghien was known for the big charcoal grill out front which resulted in juicy charred pork chops, but what I got today was the equivalent of a boiled pork chop. No smokiness, no char, no flavour, stringy and chewy. Unfortunately it was inedible. Sorry to leave a bad review like this, but hope this is a wake up call - from a 13 year customer. Com tam van cu is definitely better.

author: Michael Vu
review_text: One of the best broken-rice (Cơm Tấm) in Saigon. The portion is quite big, but tasty grilled pork ribs are great to try.

author: russell ng
review_text: We grabbed this meal and it was very good. I really wanted to get some broken rice on this trip and I was very pleased with this meal. The pork chop is huge. It’s so big and the meal was so good. One of my favourites honestly and I think that I need to get this meal on this trip again because it was so good unfortunately we only had one time and we were crabbing in all these different meals so we’d have time to go to the actual restaurant as you can see me splitting apart this meal in the hotel but I recommend either going to the actual restaurant and getting it fresh or just getting the delivery like we did

author: Kody Kai
review_text: There was a lot of buzz around this place so we decided to try it. We got the chicken broken rice and the pork broke rice. Our food came out in no more than 2 minutes. The only part of our dishes that were hot, was the rice. The meat was room temperature. If this plate was hot, I would have easily given it 5 stars. It’s also weird because we arrived about 10 minutes after opening.

author: Sarena Nicole Arokiasamy
review_text: My friends and I had a great time at Cơm Tấm Ba Ghiền! The place was packed, but we were still able to find a table without much trouble. The food was served right away, and everything was delicious with generous portions. I absolutely loved the chico fruit shake — highly recommended! On top of that, the customer service was friendly and attentive, which made the experience even better.

author: Jan Exar Aspiras
review_text: Food is good. but the Quantity is really plenty. We ordered #5, and it should be sufficient for 2-3 person.

author: Ben Yee
review_text:
Had the option 5 on the menu, which is mixed, the price is at 166k VND, which is on the pricier side.
Portion wise generous, the pork chop is huge and well marinated. Would recommend to go for option 2 which consist of the pork chop and fried egg, that would be sufficient, as I don’t find the mixed option to be very worth it as the star here is the pork chop.

author: Laura Witty
review_text: 2 out of our 4 got horrible food poisoning from it. So gnarly we lost an entire day as we were so sick we couldn’t leave the hotel. I would have rated it higher because it was delicious and the service was great but I want to save someone from getting raging sick. For context we’ve been in country 2 weeks and haven’t had anything remotely to tummy troubles. This was full blown food poisoning.

author: lordminder
review_text: Absolute waste of time and waste of money. Went with viet friends , everyone found the meal inedible. Ox tails were tiny. It's impossible to chew and had little to no meat. Young was not cooked correctly. Chewy and impossible to eat. Brisket was chewy full of inedible veins and fat. Tendons were undercooked and in edible. Had to throw the entire meal away. Avoid this place. Many other local places that are far superior. *pictures attached.

author: Santos Gil
review_text: I really enjoy eating here. The food is consistently good, the restaurant is neat and tidy, and the staff are always cheerful and professional.

author: Evan Lee
review_text:
This beef hotpot is surprisingly good! The cold weather in December made us want something warm and comforting and Googling around, we decided to try this spot out. The place was absolutely packed and we waited about 5 minutes to get a table. Everything on the menu looked great and we tried the pickled chicken feet and pork ears. It was really good and not overpowering like most places. Next we tried the self-grill goat boobs (yes, goat boobs) and it was also really good. It's pre-marinated so you don't need to dip anything else. And last but not least is their signature Mongolian beef hotpot. Packed with meat and about $12USD for two, the hotpot was amazingly good. The broth and dipping sauces were on point. Everything was really good and service was fast and friendly. I would definitely come back and recommend this place!

Update:
Fourth time visiting and it's still as good as day one. They're even more busy than before as we went on a Sunday evening and the restaurant is packed. Quality has not suffered one bit. Definitely one of the best beef hotpots in Da Nang and our favorite for sure.
Boil it well before eating. People with weak immunity should be especially careful. Hygiene can’t really be trusted here...

author: Lan Pham
review_text:
Got drawn in by a TikTok video. Ordered the Mongolian hotpot. Meat and veggies were acceptable quality, though there was some dirt on the bok choy and I didn't care for the mystery meat bits in the tripe balls. Broth was too sweet.
Ambiance was ok. Tables were too low.
Service was ok.
₫300k for the hotpot and two Hudas.
One and done for us, but those who like sugary savory dishes might like this place.

author: Công Minh Vũ
review_text:
Food:
- The food is decent, the broth has a good flavor.

- Many beef dishes for hot pot are good.

Service:

- Fast service.

- Affordable prices.

Atmosphere:

- The restaurant is clean and has some decor.

- Located on a main road, convenient transportation.

- Not too noisy.

- It's a narrow building, a bit cramped. The restaurant is small, not very spacious.

author: Ngoc Anh Nguyen
review_text: The grilled food was a bit oily and felt a bit greasy. The hot pot was sweet and easy to eat, with a huge chunk of beef. The chicken feet were given as a gift. The price was not expensive and the road was easy to get to.

author: Vĩnh Phúc Khánh Đoan
review_text:
I recently visited O Ty Beef Hotpot on 2/9 Street, ordered a beef hotpot set for 2 people and felt very satisfied with the experience. The hotpot portion was quite full, including many types of soft, delicious, very fresh and high-quality beef. The hotpot broth was moderately sweet, eaten with fresh vegetables and side dishes, making the meal more appealing. 

The restaurant space is spacious, clean, has cool air conditioning, very comfortable to sit for a long time and enjoy. 

What impressed me most was the feeling of fullness after the meal, a lot of meat but still retains its delicious softness, just like a standard beef hotpot. The price is reasonable, suitable for the quality of food and the space of the restaurant.

author: Phượng Vũ
review_text: My first impression was that the broth was quite similar to pho broth, without any unique characteristics. I don’t know if the restaurant used a lot of MSG, but the broth tasted quite sweet. After finishing the meal, my friend felt his throat was a bit smooth. I ordered a hot pot set for 2-3 people for 189k, there was a promotion for an extra plate of chicken feet or mixed jellyfish. I found the dipping sauce to be delicious, but the chao was normal.

author: Sao Vang Da Nang
review_text:
🇻🇳 Nice local Vietnamese hotpot restaurant. They seem to always be busy so staff can be a little bit slow and they didn’t get our order exactly right.

But the food is good, well priced, and the portions are appropriately sized.

Busy location so better to sit inside to avoid the traffic noise if you can get a table there.

author: Jannah
review_text: Both the beef hot pot and the butter-grilled meat were delicious; the meat was fresh and the portions were generous. The waiters were also warm and friendly.

author: Banana
review_text: If you're looking for a Vietnamese shabu-shabu experience with a local twist, this is the place to go. The broth is especially delicious. The meat wrapped in a thin layer of scallion is also delicious.

author: 유지원
review_text: Communication with the staff was difficult due to language barriers, but we proactively used a translator to resolve the issue. I'm not familiar with the country's cuisine, so I can't comment on the taste, but it might be a matter of personal preference. Nevertheless, I thoroughly enjoyed every bit of the meal.

author: Bui Nga (Kelly Bui)
review_text:
🌟 **O Ty Beef Hotpot - Rich Flavor, Dedicated Service** 🌟

O Ty Beef Hotpot is truly an ideal destination for those who love delicious and rich beef hotpot. The hotpot broth is clear but the flavor is extremely well-rounded, making me remember it every time I enjoy it. The grilled dishes dipped in fermented bean curd are also very delicious, creating a special and unforgettable flavor.

The staff here are very friendly and dedicated, always ready to serve customers with a smile on their faces. However, the restaurant needs to pay more attention to keeping the space clean to create the best experience for diners.

Overall, O Ty beef hotpot deserves to be a great choice for gatherings with friends and family. Come and enjoy, you will not be disappointed!

author: Hoang Tram
review_text:
I was a victim when I went to eat according to the reviewer. The 5 of us all had the same comment:
The beef hotpot stinks, the tripe is not crispy, the fish sauce is too sweet, the beef tongue is the most disappointing dish, it is unimaginably soft, I have eaten at several beef hotpot restaurants, and this is the most disappointing restaurant I have ever eaten, when paying the bill I told the waiter about the tongue dish, but he did not respond.
I have to review so that others do not become victims like me 😭 A truly wasted meal. The dish that was okay was the mixed beef tendon, which was okay. 🙉
And of course we will never come back to this restaurant. A table of 5, we left with great disappointment. You asked why we ate everything. Because we were sorry for the money. There is no way we would come back or recommend others to eat at this restaurant.

author: Mizu NTT
review_text:
The first thing to mention is: Very dirty
Secondly, it's the service of the staff

My group went on Saturday night. We waited for a long time but no staff came to ask anything. We called 2-3 times before the staff came.
We ordered a special hot pot but the vegetables were a bit dirty. I asked "Hey, is this really the vegetables for the special hot pot?" The staff replied "yes" and turned away. A while later, a friend brought out another plate of vegetables to exchange, but the vegetable plate had a snail on it. We asked them to wash the vegetables again. Then they brought out a different plate of vegetables :)

Next is the dipping sauce, there were 5 people but they gave us 4 bowls of hot pot dipping sauce. When we ordered grilled food, there was no sauce or dipping sauce as the tiktoker reviews said

The staff's attitude was terrible, they were negligent and didn't take care of the customers. They answered customers curtly. Especially the guy with the buzz cut and earrings (probably the manager or owner). The customers were still sitting and eating at the restaurant, but he was humming and singing like there was no one around :)

There were also rats crawling around. NEVER COME BACK

author: Phuong Nhu
review_text:
I've always been hesitant about hot pot with its strong beef fat smell, but I stumbled upon this restaurant and their Mongolian-style beef hot pot was surprisingly delicious. The broth was sweet and savory, and the vegetables were incredibly tasty. The pan-fried beef tripe and braised oxtail were also excellent.
The only downside is that the tables are low and the stools aren't very comfortable.

author: Do Thao
review_text: Compared to many other restaurants, my taste at this restaurant is the best, the price is cheap. I went with the hot pot program for 1, 2 people for only 99k + grilled combo for 139k, but 3 people were full, there was a lot of meat, I ate a lot. The male waiters were quick. The only thing is that the restaurant was crowded so it was a bit hot.

author: Kim Thủy Bùi
review_text: Airy, clean tables and chairs, very fresh meat, reasonable price and a lot of food.

author: Trúc Nguyễn
review_text: The beef hotpot restaurant has no faults, everyone! It meets the criteria, delicious and cheap. My family ordered a beef hotpot and received a plate of boneless chicken feet and mixed tendons. Braised beef intestines with green pepper. Grilled beef with salted egg sauce.

author: María MF
review_text:
Very nice staff and delicious food. Very fresh fish and seafood and cheaper than others.
The problem is that they take so much time to bring the food. Almost an hour for one piece of fish…

author: Chong Delon
review_text: Anything you order, will be worth your penny. Seafoods and fishes are fresh. Portion is huge. Very very local place and vibes. You know it's a great place when there is not much tourist hanging around. A gem place to visit.

author: Igo Grego
review_text: Recommended by the lady in the pharmacy. Then i walked in to the restaurant. Seafood was really good, especially the shrimp 🦐 Many Locals are dine here

author: Dewi D
review_text: This restaurant serves very fresh seafood and the owner was so helpful with suggestion. Our seafood dishes were steamed with ginger n garlic sauce to bring out the sweetness of fresh seafood. Price point is also reasonable. This restaurant is a come back.

author: Rocky Mok
review_text: Amazing good value local spot, and very tasty! The seafood has lots of variety….! And service is great. Good comes out fast, even when it’s packed!!

author: Ori Joy
review_text:
Wide variety of fresh live seafood, You can choose from 3 methods of cooking - steamed, fried or grilled. Our family love all the dishes as the seafood is fresh and cooked well.
There are 2 seating areas- indoors and outdoors. Due to a passing shower, the indoor area was quite packed. We can tell that this restaurant is popular among the locals. There’s a menu for foreigners but I’m not sure how fluent in English are the waiters; we told our guide what we wanted and he helped us speak to the waiter.
Overall, a satisfactory dinner

author: Thanh Ly
review_text:
Da Nang has hundreds of seafood restaurants and it's easy to get overwhelmed by the sheer number of restaurants offering fresh/live seafood. We were very fortunate that this restaurant was 7 minutes from our Airbnb. We found it while we were pushing our little boy around so he could fall asleep for his afternoon nap. This restaurant also happened to be on my list of researched places to eat, so we decided to try it out once the boy had fallen asleep. The restaurant wasn't particularly busy but we were between meals 4pm. It's a big restaurant and there were 5 tables, all locals. When the food arrived, we knew right away the quality was fantastic and the seafood fresh. The service was beyond fantastic, my wife wanted a fresh coconut, something they didn't offer but the staff went down the street and bought one, charged us the cost of the coconut only and not extra for the service (we paid 25k VND for it). We got a mixture of clams, one booked with lemongrass and chilli and the other in a coconut sauce, both absolutely delicious. We also got the Thai squid and papaya salad, which was as good as you'd get in Thailand.

The restaurant was so good we have been there now 3 times in 4 days. One for lunch and twice for dinner, bringing my Vietnamese parents along with us. They really rate the good and I think we've tried pretty much all of their fresh seafood so far, we haven't had a disappointing dish yet. Our boy loves the chicken, which unfortunately does take about an hour as they cook it fresh and the minimum order is half a chicken. Works well for take away as he eats it late in the evening or in the morning.

This is very much a local joint, the locals love it and for good reason. They dishes are fantastic and cooked right. Beer will cost you 17k VND for a bottle of Saigon beer. It's about 70% cheaper than Lang Ca (the famous seafood restaurant in Da Nang, avoid it like the plague), and much cheaper than any of the beach side seafood restaurants. We were there on Tuesday night and the place was rammed. Tour buses turn up and go to the place opposite, this restaurant doesn't need to rely on that business as they get so busy with the locals. They do have an English menu, so ordering shouldn't be a problem. The staff are fantastic and they go above and beyond to make customers feel at home. It's a big and clean restaurant.

And despite what other reviews have said, it's not a Thai restaurant, I think they get a bit confused with the name.

I'd highly recommend this place for some great seafood, at a very, very reasonable price, where you are experiencing the local vibe. You won't be disappointed.

author: Ching San Lim
review_text: So this was our first meal after touching down in Da Nang. Our guide brought us here as we said we only wanted to go where locals go and this was it. Every dish that we ordered was excellent and the best part of the service included pealing our mantis and sea prawns at the side for us so that all we needed to do was to open our mouth and chew. Definitely highly recommend this place 👍👍👍

author: Yvonne Ng
review_text: Fresh seafood. We tried steam prawns, steam fish, clams and fried rice. Excellent taste. Recommended by our local tour guide. Price is reasonable. Highly recommended.

author: 햄벅
review_text:
It is not right next to the sea, but near the sea. It was a very delicious and satisfying meal. If I have a chance, I really want to go again.

한국인들 집합해야되는 곳
맛집

author: Markéta Jenčková
review_text: Overall a good experience. We had stir fry noodles with beef and it was delicious, the meat was cooked very nicely so we enjoyed that.

author: Lokesha Haber
review_text: You get to choose your fish or seafood directly, along with your preferred preparation method—grilled, steamed, sashimi, etc. Prices per kilogram are clearly displayed on each of the many fish tanks, and they confirm the total cost with you before cooking. The preparation was excellent, and the price was extremely reasonable. Yet another spot recommended by locals, and it definitely lived up to the reputation!

author: Trân P
review_text: Food is little below average. The seafood noodles is completely a lie and disappointment, only four small shrimps in there and they call it seafood?? The hotpot was low quality too. The oysters rather old and not fresh.Would not recommend it

author: Daniel Oppa
review_text: 250314 It's a low-cost food, but you need to be patient if you want to eat it after ordering.

author: Nino Kiers
review_text: The food was delicious! But the staff seemed really stressed out, as it was very busy. They forgot about some of our dishes which they then ran out of, and they added an extra dish to the receipt that we did not get. But they were really nice about it and refunded us immediately.

author: Z D Y
review_text:
Went as a tour. Atmosphere is good and inviting.

Food was ok. Good presentation. Service was ok. They cant speak english, abit of communication breakdown. Seafood is fresh.

author: Sathesh
review_text: Food was very nice especially if the cooking method is BBQ. The staff are friendly and very helpful especially when peeling the lobsters and the prawns. Price is there to see..

author: Douglas Whitcombe
review_text: Grilled Tiger Prawns and Oysters washed down with a Tiger hit the spot. Off the main waterfront strip so prices were reasonable

author: BDR Albadar
review_text: If you’re in da nang and you want try best seafood in local restaurants with good prices try this place so delicious food

author: M C
review_text:
Da Nang local restaurant near Mike Beach.
It is near the back of Hilton Hotel.
I think it was the freshest and cheapest seafood restaurant near the beach.
I visited on Saturday and there were a lot of people
There were many kind steps, so it wasn't uncomfortable.

restaurant: Mộc Viên - Bún Chả Hà Nội
author: Jake Yau
review_text:
What an amazing find! Tucked between shop houses, this place offers a wide variety of delicious food from Hanoi.
I ordered bun cha, which was so delicious! Sauce was perfect and the grilled meat was smokey and savory.
Also ordered some fried spring rolls and coconut white coffee; all were delicious.
Do come here to enjoy their hospitality, friendliness and obviously the amazing food!

restaurant: Mộc Viên - Bún Chả Hà Nội
author: Todd Moon
review_text: I just moved to this area and found this nice Bun Cha shop. It is a nice quiet area and has plenty of on street parking. The Bun Cha was very good and we ordered a side of egg rolls. They had a couple cats that wanted to be friends in the indoor seating area.

restaurant: Mộc Viên - Bún Chả Hà Nội
author: Mr. Jo
review_text: nice atmosphere. fair prices. friendly staff. order to go or good for brekkie, brunch, lunch. note the opening hours 6am-2pm. banh mi is basic & good. menu see pics below.

restaurant: Mộc Viên - Bún Chả Hà Nội
author: Butch Recibe
review_text: The price is very affordable. The place is cozy, the food is really really great. The free soup is very delicious. The Banh Mi was my favorite. They use pure meat.

restaurant: Mộc Viên - Bún Chả Hà Nội
author: Anie Koltsova
review_text: Everything we tried here was delicious! Excellent hospitable service. Friendly atmosphere. Ate here almost every day during our vacation, occasionally twice a day haha. That’s how tasty it is. Cards, qr code, cash payments — all options are available.

restaurant: Mộc Viên - Bún Chả Hà Nội
author: Oi L W
review_text:
We recently visited this restaurant near our apartment on two occasions within just three days, and it was a happy experience! 😸

The banh mi sandwiches are good and have a comforting, homey feel. However, we wish they had a bit more filling, as we prefer them thick like homemade versions. 😂

The spring rolls are deep-fried, so expect them to be a bit oily. We're not huge fans of deep-fried foods, so our comments are neutral. They aren't overly salty and have no strange flavors, making them a decent comfort food option, especially when paired with warm rice.

The pho (noodle soup) is made with a clear broth that’s perfect for breakfast or dinner. It’s a versatile meal that’s easy to enjoy at any time. If you're planning to order, go for the large bowl—it offers great value without being overwhelming in size. ❤️

The salt coffee is decent as well. ☕

We haven't tried the bun cha yet, but we're excited to do so next time! The grilled meat looks incredibly flavorful, though we’re a bit intimidated by how to eat it.

Overall, a lovely spot we look forward to returning to! 😘

restaurant: Mộc Viên - Bún Chả Hà Nội
author: Eddy Lin
review_text: Good food with cute puppy. Lady boss was very nice, speaks English well, and honest. I almost paid 10 times the amount with cash and she corrected me. Price was very reasonable too.

restaurant: Mộc Viên - Bún Chả Hà Nội
author: Snir
review_text:
Pho is tasty, too bad the waiter didn't serve the complimentary greens and leaves along with the dish.
while the edible meat parts were delicious, most of the protein served was pure fat I couldn't eat

restaurant: Mộc Viên - Bún Chả Hà Nội
author: 보디사트바
review_text: I went because I was in front of the hotel. It was the best banh mi I had in Vietnam. and I was walking by and they greeted me, but I didn't know you were doing this to me. smile is so beautiful.

restaurant: Mộc Viên - Bún Chả Hà Nội
author: Darren Meredith
review_text: It’s a really quiet hidden gem … staff are really friendly and attentive prices are good and  location is quiet although a little messy.  Can get away from the beeping and enjoy beer with your food.   Living in Thailand I do miss a good baguette and they didn’t disappoint.

restaurant: Mộc Viên - Bún Chả Hà Nội
author: David Popperfield
review_text:
My favourite dish from Hanoi.

Glad to be able to try it here, although I wish for the soup to be slightly more tangy. Overall, the grill pork and pork cake were delicious. Perfectly charred and marinated.

They have both outdoor and indoor areas.

Staffs were friendly and hospitable! Will definitely recommend and come back again

restaurant: Mộc Viên - Bún Chả Hà Nội
author: Victoria
review_text:
We tried the small-sized pho bo — and it was absolutely delicious! 😍 The broth was rich and flavorful, with thin slices of beef. We also had the banh mi with pork — there was plenty of meat, everything was juicy and tasty. And the sweetest dog welcomed us 🐶 — such a lovely touch!

Thank you so much for the amazing food and warm atmosphere 😊

restaurant: Mộc Viên - Bún Chả Hà Nội
author: Matt Gibson
review_text: Great food for a great price and awesome staff. I'm staying in a hotel around the corner and have been eating here everyday at least once, sometimes twice, for a week and I will come back every day until I leave. Fantastic spot.

restaurant: Mộc Viên - Bún Chả Hà Nội
author: Clara
review_text:
a quaint little store and a simple menu (pho + bun cha + spring rolls of various flavors). they don’t have many staff so be prepared to wait a bit for your food. friendly staff too!

loved the seafood spring roll:)

the medium sized pho is on the smaller side so would advise to upsize to large.

restaurant: Mộc Viên - Bún Chả Hà Nội
author: Marblelr
review_text:
I haven’t tried the pho yet, but the bun cha here is legit — clean, tasty, and pretty true to the original flavor. Definitely makes it into my top 2 or 3 favorite spots for bun cha.

Prices are reasonable, and the owner (from the North) runs the place with great service and a warm, friendly attitude. Nothing to complain about — I was actually quite satisfied.

The place was recommended to me by a foreign friend, and I’ve heard good things from other expat friends too. Definitely worth a try!

restaurant: Mộc Viên - Bún Chả Hà Nội
author: Umami Ngon
review_text: Pleasantly pleased with our pho - broth was flavorful and noodles were smooth.  Guava juice was refreshing.  The staff were very friendly and attentive.  A small puppy entertained us while waiting for our meals.  Will definitely come back to try their spring rolls and bun cha.

restaurant: Mộc Viên - Bún Chả Hà Nội
author: Sergey O
review_text:
This is my go-to place for pho bo. The flank pieces are tender, and the rich flavor of the broth feels so right. Then you get sprouted beans and some greens, which are just wonderful additions.
In the picture, you see a medium-sized bowl, which is only 35k right now, and I asked not to add any onion/spiciness.
Organ-lemongrass juice is rich in flavor and feels refreshing.
The people who run this place are friendly, and the service is fantastic.
The only downside I can think of is the flies, but that comes with an open space. The place is well-maintained.

restaurant: Mộc Viên - Bún Chả Hà Nội
author: The_leader
review_text:
It's delicious~
The price is low.
The portions are generous!

restaurant: Mộc Viên - Bún Chả Hà Nội
author: B K
review_text:
Pleasantly surprised with the food. The place is definitely a hidden gem 💎.  I'd say that's the freshest Pho I have tried in Vietnam. I could taste multiple flavours and the beef was perfectly cooked. Comfortable tables and chairs as well as nicer chop sticks than most places generally.  It's a peaceful environment and quiet too. The owner takes care of their restaurant well, it's clean. Will definitely re-visit!

Note: The lady that served us also speaks very good English which is rare. Great hospitality and customer skills.

restaurant: Mộc Viên - Bún Chả Hà Nội
author: WILSON WONG
review_text: Fantastic! Very good beef noodle, very good french bread, very good spring roll, great Vietnamese coffee, sooooooo yummy!  Just love it 👏🏻👏🏻

author: Chengjie WANG
review_text:
I've been here twice, and overall, it’s been a great dining experience.

All the pizzas are made to order, and it takes about 15 to 20 minutes for them to be served after placing your order. Watching the guys working busily at the oven adds to the whole vibe.

The freshness of the food is pretty good. The squid ink rice is tender and comes with a skewer of springy squid meat, which is quite nice.

For pizzas, you can order half-and-half. I recommend the Burrata Parma Ham flavor—the parma ham adds a savory taste, while the creamy cheese brings a rich texture, all on a crispy thin crust. The combination of flavors and textures is very satisfying. The cheese pizza is also good. The table comes with honey, which you can drizzle on top. Two slices of pizza are enough to leave you feeling content.

The tuna salad is fresh and tasty, though the portion is a bit small.

For drinks, they serve beer with meals, about 250ml per glass. I wouldn’t recommend the Da Lat Whey Stout—it lacks the rich, bold taste of a stout. The honey wine beer, on the other hand, is great—it’s quite sweet and very drinkable.

The only issue is that there’s often a queue. If you don’t make a reservation in advance, you might have to wait even after arriving. I once saw someone come at 2 p.m., only to be told they could only get a table at 4 p.m. They left looking disappointed, and I’m not sure if they ever came back.

Alternatively, you could ride a motorbike here and, if there’s a wait, take a stroll to the nearby Pink Church or the My Son Sculpture Museum, which are just a few hundred meters away. Time will fly by before you know it.

The My Son Sculpture Museum is truly amazing! But that’s another story.

By the way, Ngoc provides a very good service as well.

author: Morgana Lamb
review_text:
Food was amazing. We ordered the burrata Parma Margherita and the 5 cheese pizza and it was delicious. The staff were very friendly and kind. Delivered the order so quick, was impressed. Prices are great and service wonderful. I really recommend this place!

We did not have a table reserved as we found this place last minute but they gently accommodated us at the bar and we had a brilliant experience. 10/10

author: Sean Hyland
review_text:
We had a very nice meal in Pizza 4Ps. The meat in the spaghetti bolognaise was excellent, so was the pizza. Tiramisu was also very tasty.

The service was great, everyone was so friendly.

Just thought the portion sizes were on the smaller side, considering the more expensive prices compared to other restaurants. Bill is the last photo.

author: jayne lee
review_text:
Came to 4P pizza twice during my trip to Danang. People told me it's overrated but i beg to differ. The quality of the ingredients were so good, price point is decent, the service staffs attention to details were immaculate! Best part was they allowed half & half pizza flavours and have options of Small or Large Burrata!

Tried the bolognese pasta, crab pasta, tiramisu, panna cotta.
Pizza flavours we had Large burrata parma ham on both days, another flavour was salmon miso and the other was scallop gratin.

totally recommended to drizzle the honey and chilli oil on their burrata pizza! It will make a huge difference

Staffs were very well train as upon ordering the panna cotta they will mention that the fruits will be sour and they let you decide :) they also provided wait time of pasta/pizzas.

Counter seats are totally recommended if you like to watch how they do their operations.

author: Marina Jethrine Castro
review_text:
