I think this Pho Ga and Mien Ga was the best bowl in my life, also in Vietnam. Last time, I could not recognize because of lack of my experience, but after I had so many popular noodles all over the Vietnam, I can recognize. I want to come back again.

author: Rachael Wong
review_text: Delicious bowl of chicken pho, broth is very rich and flavorful. Tender chicken, fresh herbs, just right. A bit far out, but worth the trip. Service is friendly, place stays clean.

author: Abbie Diem
review_text: The food was good, they don’t use too much sugar so the broth is not too sweet. The portions are small though. The chicken meat is firm.

author: Celine T
review_text: My personal favourite in HCMC. I’ve been here 3 times now - the first back in 2023 and it was life changing. The chicken pho is just as good 2 years later. It is chicken soup for the soul manifested in real life. I’ll continue dreaming of the day I can have this pho again.

author: Irene
review_text: This is a must-visit place for me every time in HCM. I went back so many times during my trip there. The soup and the chicken tasted perfectly. Can’t wait to come back!!

author: Irene F
review_text: Love the soup noodles and the salad. You can choose your noodles with the same soup base. Our group chose the glass noodles, thin egg noodles and pho noodles. We loved the chicken salad with lotus root and banana blossoms.

author: RYSA
review_text: the pho broth was unimpressive, saw many good reviews but was disappointed with it. tasted like MSG, doesnt taste good at all compared to other phos i have tried in hcmc. maybe try once is good but will not come back again for the pho

author: Richard
review_text: Perfect for a rainy day. Got the chicken pho and vermicelli. Both were good. Chicken salad was also very good. I do wish the broth had a slightly stronger chicken flavour.

author: 招财喵
review_text:
The Michelin recommend chicken pho.
The taste is just ok for me, not a must to visit, their homemade chili sauce is nice!

author: Yee Win Maw
review_text:
Pho but only chicken.
Taste 9/10
A little but far from city center
If you want to try pho and don’t eat beef, this is one of the options.

author: Che P
review_text: The staff are very attentive, Pho Mien Ga has amazing flavors, the clear broth is very savory, and the chicken is very juicy 10/10 experience. They don't speak English, but they are very welcoming to foreigners. Also, they accept cash only. Cash is king in Vietnam.

author: Joey Lu
review_text:
Had a super shiok meal at Phở Miến gà Kỳ Đồng.

We ordered the pho with chicken breast, egg noodles, and a chicken salad to share.

The broth was light but full of flavour, and the chicken was fresh and tender. The herbs and bean sprouts added a nice crunch, really made the bowl more satisfying.

The chicken salad was refreshing, got a good mix of herbs and onions. The iced black coffee was strong, just nice to finish off the meal. Place has a nice local feel, very straightforward, busy but no fuss.

Just take note it’s cash only, so better bring enough.

Will definitely come back for another bowl when I’m around in Vietnam.

author: Katharina Brandau
review_text: Awesome coffee place in HCMC, if you are into speciality coffee. Staff take their coffee seriously. They give great recommendations and show their different brewing methods and utensils. The place itself is on the 3rd floor, industrial design and nice decor. Loved it so much that we took a 20min walk just to come back here for a nice V60. Got beans, too.

author: Ann Ng
review_text:
☕ The Workshop has a cool industrial-style interior with spacious seating and plenty of natural light. The bar is lined with coffee equipment, creating a professional vibe — a great spot for coffee lovers.

This is my third visit, and the food and drinks are still up to standard:
• Pour-over coffee: aromatic, smooth, and beautifully presented.
• Omelette with toast & salad: fluffy, tasty, and just the right portion.
• Croissant: crisp, buttery, and perfect with jam and butter.

The only downside is that the staff don’t seem very welcoming — a warmer smile and friendliness would make the experience even better.

Overall, still a great place to enjoy coffee, breakfast, or brunch. 🌟

author: Janine Chang
review_text:
great cafe on the 3rd or 4th floor (can't remember which exactly). they seat you and present the menu for you to select from. the prices are a little higher, though they take their coffee seriously so it's definitely for those with a high appreciation of coffee. everything we had there was delicious! my sister-in-law isn't a coffee person but loves tiramisu and loved theirs.

they have a restroom on the same floor, outside of the cafe.

author: Polevy Ezekiel
review_text: One of the most recommended specialty coffee shop in Ho Chi Minh called @theworkshopcoffee, established since 2014 and located in the bustling Bến Nghé area. Located on the second floor of an old 1912 building, the classic vintage ambience feels very strong because many architectural elements are very well maintained. High ceilings with many window openings from various directions create good natural lighting, causing a warm, comfy and welcoming space. Various coffee menus are served here and the ones I recommend most are classic coffee and manual brew with various of the best coffee beans from various origins.

author: Leonard Lim
review_text:
Workshop Coffee in Ho Chi Minh City is one of those places that stands out for its cool, industrial-chic vibe. It’s always lively and full of energy, popular with Chinese tourists and expats alike. Their coffee is excellent, and although the food menu is quite limited, everything I’ve tried has been tasty.

The only downsides for me are that the entrance is a bit hidden—you have to go up a flight of stairs to find it—and it can get really crowded and noisy during busy hours. Also, I personally find the chairs quite uncomfortable, which makes it hard to sit for long.

author: Giovanni
review_text: Definitely the place where to have nice food and where to work at a laptop. They're built for that, there are plugs everywhere and the wifi is strong. The staff will not bother you, but it's good habit to order something every hour at least, and tip the staff appropriately. The food is good, big, and vote expensive. Good quality place.

author: Chuin Ling Ung (CL)
review_text: It's a quite hidden kind of cafe if you don't really notice the signboard. It's kinda cute though. The variety of coffee served here are really special and are so good. Tried their nutty cremina and salted iced coffee, and I can say the salted iced coffee is a must try! Panna cotta gives off a very balanced taste and it's really good.

author: Dallas D
review_text:
A beautiful loft-style space with true European vibes — spacious, high ceilings, great light. As someone who loves lofts, I felt right at home.

Built a couple of documents here and genuinely enjoyed the atmosphere.

Excellent espresso, and big thanks to the team for creating such a well-designed environment for focus and creativity.🫶

author: Chlotus
review_text: This is a lovely little cafe where we can take a break from our walking tour! It's tucked away in a building, giving it a cozy feel. The coffee here is delicious and has a nice strong flavor. It's a popular spot for people working or studying, but it's a bit too quiet, almost like a library.

author: S Marie
review_text: Nice café with a good view and fine for a quick stop, but the drinks were disappointing. I asked for Vietnamese coffee for my latte, and they didn’t have it, which was surprising. The baristas also weren’t flexible with adjusting the sweetness or replacing the sweet milk with fresh milk. The service was okay, but the overall experience was average at best.

author: piglene
review_text: came here to complete some work. i think the chair is a bit painful to sit in for a long time. it was a bit difficult to find the cafe since it is through a small corridor and up the stairs but it really feels like a hidden gem. a friendly local street vendor had to help us and point us to the cafe to find it. plenty of electrical plugs available and the staff with provide you a multi plug if you need it! it is just the right temperature but gets really really noisy when it starts raining 😭 i enjoyed the food! the service is perfect for introverts. not much smiles and attention but they will help you immediately if you asked for it!

author: Gildwen LE FERREC
review_text: A known place for the coffee drinkers. Great busy-coffee « bar » where one can meet friends, do some coworking in dedicated spots, enjoy the taste of coffee and learn new grain type and tastes. They have great food as well and really offer a precise coffee making. Highly recommend!

author: Lionel Sim
review_text:
I visited The Working Coffee recently and left dissatisfied with the service experience.

Service was slow from ordering to drink delivery, despite the café not being overly busy. The staff member handling my order, Vy, appeared overwhelmed and uncoordinated with the rest of the team. There was visible confusion behind the counter, with staff moving in overlapping paths and frequently bumping into one another.

There was also no clear or systematic ordering process. Customers were unsure where to queue or who was responsible for taking orders. Tasks seemed to shift between staff members without clear ownership, which contributed to delays and disrupted workflow.

The café has potential, but the lack of structured operations and clear staff coordination significantly impacted the experience. A defined ordering system, clearer role assignment, and better internal communication would improve service efficiency and customer flow.

author: Ming Dao
review_text:
This has been one of my go-to coffee shops since the early days of specialty coffee in Vietnam. After 9 years, it still feels the same.

Great coffee. Delicious food. A space that strikes a quiet balance, not too loud, not too quiet. The large windows open to a beautiful city view

More than just a coffee, it’s a place that still carries the spirit of old Saigon

author: Miley Cyrus
review_text: It wasn’t very easy for me to find the entrance, I at first thought I’m at a wrong place, but look at the entrance in my pictures if u got confused like me😹 I paid 175.000vnd for this omelette 🍳 prices are about 45-100 for the drinks and 130-200 for the food.  it’s a bit expensive for me but it was delicious and cooked very fast. I recommend this place to visit 👍🏻 u can bring ur computer and work here but today around 6pm it was a bit crowdy. It’s not quiet but also not noisy.

author: Hazel Ta
review_text:
Very mid if not tasteless coffee (latte) and non-coffee (oolong cold brew) drinks 😰

The ambience was amazing which is why the ratings got 3* and why we even came back. Metal chairs with limited support for your back so it will get uncomfy for long sitting and somehow the tables are super low??? (I’m not even that tall…)

Staffs were unwelcoming and borderline rude to Vietnamese customers, when we came in it was crowded and they told us to sit at the large shared table despite having a vacant window-side table. They put the reserve sign on it, but when we about to leave a female staff came and said we could sit there (?). I paid 200k for 2 mid drinks and 1 cookie yet they were annoyed when we ask for our free parking tickets 🥀??? Much better support and hospitality for other Non-Viet customers

Guess this is one of those places that only welcomes foreigners like the ones in Thao Dien =)))

author: Tommy Tang
review_text: This place is wildly famous! Though the street-level sign is so small you'd easily miss it. Entering the first floor feels like walking into a condemned building. You'll need to navigate narrow, steep stairs up to the third floor. The coffee and cakes? Decent but forgettable. The staff are lovely though - which almost makes up for the completely uninspired food.

author: Asli Leone
review_text: Great spot for breakfast and getting some laptop work done with a solid cappuccino. It’s spacious, with power outlets, reliable Wi-Fi, and decaf coffee available. It tends to get busy after 10 a.m., so if you need a quieter atmosphere, it’s best to go early when they open at 8.

author: Billy Fyfe
review_text: Great place…tough to find, you have to go up three floors but that’s normal in Vietnam, I love it. Definitely recommended. Good coffee and the Benedict was perfect.

author: David Nguyen
review_text: Great place for digital nomads looking to do some work. Great views near the windows and lots of coffee options from pour over to specialty flavors.

author: Dani Calvo
review_text: this food was incredible. favorite dish was definitely the bep cuon combo 2. the pork and shrimp pancake rolled into the spring roll provided was an incredible array of flavor. we also ordered the tom su sot bo toi an kem banh bao chien, which was good as well, a little less savory than expected, but delicious. finally we ordered the Ba Chi Gion Da Mam Tac. the sauce it came with was incredible and the crispy edges of the pork were delicious. definitely recommend to stop by for a bite.

author: Bowen Chau
review_text:
Bếp Cuốn Sài Gòn is a delightful culinary gem nestled near the city center of Ho Chi Minh City, making it easily accessible via Grab. This Michelin-recommended restaurant offers a refreshing twist on traditional Vietnamese cuisine, setting it apart from the usual pho-focused menus.

Upon entering, you’re greeted by a cozy yet stylish decor that reflects a modern take on Vietnamese aesthetics. The intimate size of the restaurant fosters a warm atmosphere, perfect for enjoying a meal with friends or a loved one.

The staff at Bếp Cuốn are incredibly friendly and eager to guide you through their unique offerings. They are passionate about the menu and are happy to recommend dishes that showcase a fusion of flavors, blending classic ingredients with innovative techniques. Each dish is a testament to the chef’s creativity, bursting with fresh ingredients and vibrant tastes.

The food is nothing short of delicious, with each bite inviting you to savor the harmonious blend of textures and flavors. Overall, Bếp Cuốn Sài Gòn is a must-visit for anyone looking to experience a modern twist on Vietnamese cuisine in a welcoming setting. Don’t miss out on this unforgettable dining experience!

author: YUUKI SUGIYAMA
review_text:
My group of five stumbled upon this delightful Vietnamese restaurant in Ho Chi Minh City, and what a find it was. The decor immediately catches your eye, with its rich, traditional Vietnamese touches that make you feel truly immersed in the local culture.

Given that we didn't have any specific recommendations from social media, we decided to be adventurous and simply order whatever caught our eye from the picture menu. To our absolute delight, every single dish was a winner not a single bad choice in the lot!

A standout was the grilled pork belly. It was perfectly cooked, with a wonderfully crisp exterior that gave way to tender, juicy meat. Paired with a spicy dipping sauce, it was incredibly moreish and surprisingly light. We also thoroughly enjoyed the grilled pork with rice noodles. I’ve had this dish before in Laos, and the flavours here were just as authentic and delicious a testament to the shared culinary heritage of the region.

What makes this place even better is the price. For a group of five, we were able to enjoy a fantastic, satisfying meal without breaking the bank. A brilliant spot for anyone looking for a genuine and affordable taste of Vietnam. Highly recommended!

author: Sherilyn Tran
review_text: We stumbled upon the restaurant by chance, and it turned out to be the best decision. The food was sensational—we ordered two bánh xèo, one spring roll, and one rice soup, and everything was served without a long wait. The staff were very attentive, and the wonderful employee, Hera, showed us how to eat bánh xèo the right way! Truly the best bánh xèo I’ve ever had! Thank you for the great experience—we will definitely be back

author: R Kim
review_text: We were looking for ban xeo and saw the high ratings for Bep. Food was very good expect the chicken skewers which were dry as if they had been precooked and kept in a warming tray. Really no excuse for that. Skewers grill frairly quickly.  Other than that, the staff were very friendly and the setting was warm and inviting. Love that the wet naps were free!

author: Irene Lee
review_text: We ordered the signature platter, fried mushrooms and fried prawns. All the dishes didn't disappoint but lack the wow factor. Maybe we came with high expectations as it is a Michelin restaurant. We thought the fried mushrooms would go well with Vietnamese sauce instead of the Japanese sesame sauce. Strange to have jap sauce in a Vietnamese restaurant.

author: Lowella Tay
review_text:
We ordered the bep cuon platter as well as the bun cha and everything was amazing. Cant choose which was my favourite since all was equally good. Definitely a must try when in Ho Chi Minh!

Service from Nhu Y was also great! She showed us how to eat the banh xeo and it was very delicious.

author: Sarah Lee
review_text:
Mixed appetizer, fried chicken wings and crispy pork were good and were the only items we think were made from scratch.

The rest were just alright - stir fry beef with instant noodles, pan fried pork with frozen fries, pineapple fried rice with frozen pea and carrot mix…No draft beer

Staff were very hospitable and restaurant was well air conditioned.

Good for quick lunch stop

author: Nava Neetha
review_text:
Food here was delicious!! The flavours were fresh and bold (and loved that we could ask for free flow vegetables that were crunchy and for
more sauces). I was here 3 times in the 1 week I was in HCMC!! The service is excellent too. Would definitely recommend🤗

author: Sibu Pitse
review_text:
We had our 1st meal in Vietnam at this Michelin selected restaurant. Kai masterfully showed us how to eat the rice cakes with garden salad. Everything was fresh and absolutely delicious.
Thank you Kai for the great service.

author: Travel_Love
review_text: Food was good, but I ate better rice pancakes. I didn't like that when I asked if I can sit upstairs, the waitress told me that no because of the "rest time" (whatever it means). Then new customers came in and they allowed them to sit upstairs without any problem.

author: Jani Valkonen (JayValkyr)
review_text:
This Michelin-selected restaurant comes with high expectations. We had lunch here and it was good. Nothing exceptional, especially compared to the dinner we had last night almost by chance.

Still recommended and absolutely worth a
visit.

author: Annie. Travel and Food
review_text:
The restaurant has a charming ambiance with tasteful décor, creating a pleasant dining atmosphere. The staff were attentive and genuinely friendly, which made the experience welcoming.

As for the food, the flavors were decent, though not outstanding. Unfortunately, the seafood did not meet expectations — the squid lacked freshness and was slightly mushy, while the shrimp had a noticeable odor. The bánh xèo was flavorful but overly greasy, which made it feel heavy. The dipping sauce had a rather unusual taste that may not suit everyone’s palate.

I would still consider returning to try other dishes, hoping for a more balanced flavor and fresher ingredients next time.

author: alex kelly
review_text: Food was absolutely delicious and the staff were amazing. Specifically Hera! She went above and beyond helped show us how to eat roll the  Banh Xeo! Would highly recommend if you're traveling to Ho Chi Minh.

author: Netta Szekely
review_text: Come here if you just landed in Vietnam and want the tourist friendly version of street food. And I mean it in every good way as we came back here couple of times. Everything we ate here was delicious. Try their pre set combo plates, morning glory and pork belly. Yum.

author: Us The Creators
review_text:
platter gives you everything you need to try when you’re here! a nice restaurant to dine and try out (almost all) the vietnamese food you gotta try.

priced slightly higher than others but the food quality is good!

author: Cha Gomez
review_text: Kai (Staff) kindly granted my request for a smaller portion of Bep Cuon! The original platter for was supposed to be for sharing but I dined solo here, they modified the order and gave me 2pcs of each. Just right for me finish 🇻🇳❤️ and I did finish everything! They very much deserve the michelin recognition.

author: Osaka Nov17
review_text: Traditional Vietnamese food, the dining experience is good. Only ordered 2 dishes and a shrimp congee. Congee is sweet. The dipping sauce for steamed broccoli is tasty. Overall environment is nice.

author: Koong 8142
review_text: Fresh ingredients with a wide variety of menus. I love how the waiter took time to teach us the right way to enjoy Vietnamese Bua Sae—made the experience even more special!

author: GT Nguyen
review_text: My family of 9 came in for brunch and we had a great experience. Grandpa has a wheelchair, so we sat on the first floor. Most of Vietnam isn’t accessible, but this restaurant was as most accessible as it could be. The food was sooo good. We almost over ordered but our server informed us it might be too much food and she was right. I’m so glad they didn’t try to oversell us. The service was awesome they really care about their customers. Hera was our server and she was AMAZING! You should definitely give this place a try when you visit HCM
